title: Trump says oil and gas prices won't fall until 'right after' midterm election
content:
PresidentDonald Trumpon Wednesday saidenergyprices that have been elevated due to theIranwar will not come down until after themidterm elections, which are nearly two months away.

"Right after the election,oil pricesare going to be tumbling downward," Trump told reporters at Joint Base Andrews before heading to Texas for the Republican Party's midterm convention.

He had been asked how he plans to explain to Americans why oil prices have just soared to highs not seen since the early weeks of the war. Global benchmarkBrent crude futureson Wednesday traded above $101 per barrel for the first time since July, while U.S.West Texas Intermediate futuressurpassed $96 per barrel at session highs.

"I think it's very easy to explain to America," Trump said. "All you have to do is say, 'Will you let Iran have a nuclear weapon?' And the answer is no."

Trump also insisted that the war against Iran, now in its seventh month with no clear resolution in sight, will end "immediately after the election."

"They can't hold out any longer," said Trump, who has repeatedly claimed victory in the ongoing war, when asked to explain his prediction.

But he then suggested that Iran seeks to benefit from an election outcome unfavorable to Trump.

"They're desperate to try and affect the election, so that we can get a nice weak group of people in there, and leave them alone and let them have their nuclear weapon," the president said.

The comments amount to a rare acknowledgement from Trump that neither the war, nor the higher prices it has generated, are likely to end in the near future.

They also underscore how the protracted conflict continues to weigh down Trump and the GOP in an election cycle that has been dominated by concerns about inflation and affordability.

Trump has claimed dozens of times throughout the war that apeace dealwith Tehran is nearly at hand,only for none to emerge. But he lately appears to have given up on the prospect of a diplomatic victory, in favor of defeating Iran by destroying its military andstarving its economy.

The U.S. military said Tuesday its forces havedestroyed 10 Iranian tankersin the last week, while Iran's Revolutionary Guard has taken credit for destroying oil tankers in the Persian Gulf.

"I would say that the attacks are caused by us," Trump said, adding, "you're going to see a lot more."

Trump also claimed Wednesday thatrecord-breaking gas priceswill fall below $2 per gallon, but not until after the early November midterms — suggesting relief was still at least eight weeks away.

"I think it's going to take a little bit longer than the midterm," he said.

The remark slightly tempers Trump's recent assurance onTruth Socialthat oil prices "will drop precipitously" when the U.S. wins the war. "It will all happen quickly," he wrote.

But fuel analyst Patrick De Haan of GasBuddy said he is still skeptical of Trump's latest prediction that oil and gas prices will fall after the midterms.

"I don't see any guarantees at all of that happening," De Haan said on X.

title: Apple event 2026: Folding iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro, added AI features and more
content:
Applesaved the best for last at its biggest launch event of the yearon Wednesday, unveiling the foldable iPhone Duo.

CEOJohn Ternusmade his big debut, unveiling the iPhone 18 Pro, Airpods 5 and Apple Watch Series 12 before getting to the Duo, the company's first foldable iPhone.

Apple showcased a new set of colors for the iPhone 18, which comes in glacier and burgundy, following in the success of last year's electric Cosmic Orange colorway.

Customers are looking at a premium price for Apple's latest devices, with the iPhone 18 Pro and Max getting a $100 hike over last year's models. The foldable Duo starts at $1,999.

The company raised prices onMacs and iPadsover the summer as memory and storage costs have soared.

Big shoutout to all the readers who joined us today. Thanks for hanging out and following along with the latest announcements from Apple.

We'll have more coverage of Apple's announcements on CNBC TV with analyst and trader reactions. Watch in real time onCNBC+or theCNBC Prostream.

Apple just unveiled the C2 modem, which will power connectivity inside the folding iPhone Duo.

This is the second-generation modem Apple has made in-house, in a move that further reduces reliance on cellular modem leader Qualcomm.

"With our fully integrated approach, it's optimized to improve everyday user experiences, including using AI algorithms to improve cellular reliability, like reconnecting faster in low coverage areas," Johny Srouji, Apple's chief hardware officer, said in the keynote video.

C2 is 50% faster than Apple's previous modem, and adds 5Gmm support in the U.S. while running at 15% lower energy, according to Srouji.

Chip analyst Ben Bajarin told CNBC in an interview that Apple will likely eliminate Qualcomm chips altogether in next year's iPhone 19 line.

Apple's new introductions, including Siri AI and the iPhone Duo, failed to impress markets. For almost the entire duration of the near-80-minute presentation, the company's stock price was down.

Opening at $315.49 today, it popped briefly to $318 and then quickly dropped.

Year-to-date, the stock is up about 15%.

Apple said its iPhone duo will cost $1,999, in line with competitors and lower than much of what Wall Street was expecting.

It will hit store shelves on Oct. 23.

Apple's marketing chief Joswiak said that the outer display of the Duo was 90% the screen area of the iPhone 18 Pro, and the inner display is 7.6-inches.

The phone will use a fingerprint sensor built into the side button for unlocking. Its case is made out of titanium.

Craig Federighi, senior VP of Software Engineering, said that Apple had redesigned much of its iOS software to take advantage of the two screens, moving buttons and other controls. Users can multitask with two apps at the same time and can use Apple's stylus called Pencil.

"We looked at every aspect of iOS to see how we could make it even more useful on iPhone Duo," Federighi said.

It's official, Apple is making a foldable phone.

"For a device that plays such a central role in your life, a larger display would open up entirely new possibilities," Ternus said. "We think the best way to achieve that is with a foldable design."

He said that other foldables feel like "two phones awkwardly stuck together."

Apple's phone is about the size of a passport and has an internal and external screen.

Apple Watch did not get a price increase. Series 12 will cost $399 and up, and the Ultra 4 starts at $799. Apple also announced a new version of the Apple Watch with a ceramic case.

Apple is making its Apple Watch Series 12 into an AI device with a new feature called Audio Intelligence.

The feature will use the Apple Watch's microphone to record conversations and allow the user to review things that were just said.

"We've all been in situations where you've missed a key detail of what someone just said and wished you could go back. Now you can use live rewind, which lets you go back in time for 15 seconds," said an Apple representative in the video.

It will also be able to summarize your important conversations with a feature called Siri Recap.

"It uses ambient listening to take high-level notes of your conversations, like takeaways from a team meeting or a parent-teacher conference. Conversations will have an Apple Intelligence-generated title, summary, and key points," Apple said.

Apple said the feature would be private and would not store audio recordings or share them with Apple.

The features will be available in beta later this year.

Apple redesigned a lot of the health features in its Health iPhone app with AI-powered coaching.

"Each morning, Apple Watch analyzes your recent activity, vitals, and sleep to give you one score with a clear call on your body's capacity to take on the day," Apple's Sumbal Desai said.

It's expected to launch later this year.

Apple unveiled its new A20 Pro system on a chip for iPhone 18 Pro. It's the first high-volume smartphone processor to be made on Taiwan Semiconductor 2 nanometer, the leading chip manufacturer's most advanced node. While 2nm chips can only be made in Taiwan, Apple has committed to make some iPhone chips on TSMC's new fabs in Arizona, too.

The A20 Pro is meant to optimize AI on-device, as Apple races to catch up in the AI race by relying on the security and privacy of avoiding the cloud. The A20 Pro is a system on a chip, or SoC, with central and graphics processors and memory integrated together, and it has a dedicated AI accelerator Apple calls a Neural Engine, to optimize that AI on device.

The A20 Pro has a six-core CPU that Apple said runs up to 20% faster, with neural accelerators to power low-latency on-device AI workloads. Its new GPU has seven cores for up to a 40% increase in performance.

Memory took a big leap too, with a 50% increase in bandwidth and what Apple said is the "widest memory interface we've ever shipped in an iPhone." Apple got there by redesigning the chip to place the core logic silicon side-by-side with the memory chips.

Memory optimization is key in the midst of a global memory shortage, as all the biggest players race to secure memory supply from giants SK Hynix, Samsung and Micron. It's also why Appleraised priceson MacBooks and iPads in June.

Apple announced new AirPods models called AirPods 5.

These new devices have a longer battery life and have active noise cancellation, which previously wasn't available on the least expensive AirPods. They cost $129, and there's a version with wireless charging that retails for $149.

iOS 27 will include a new feature that allows customers to use a single phone number across multiple devices, dubbed "iPhone Handoff."

According to Kaiann Drance, vice president of iPhone Marketing, "the number is instantly active on whichever iPhone you pick up."

She added that the feature will launch with T-Mobile and Deutsche Telekom, with Verizon and EE adding support by the end of the year. More carriers will follow.

Apple's new phones will get a price increase amid a global component shortage, especially for memory.

The iPhone 18 Pro will start at $1199, Apple said. That's $100 more than last year's iPhone 17 Pro.

The iPhone 18 Pro Max will start at $1299, which is also a $100 hike.

The phones go on pre-order on Saturday and will ship on Sept. 18.

Apple introduced a new feature that will enable users to confirm that a photo was taken by an iPhone camera, instead of generated by AI. The feature is called Apple Reference Image.

"Now you can prove the authenticity of a photo taken on iPhone 18 Pro. Apple Reference Image starts in the most secure way possible with the sensor. The new main camera securely signs photo data at a pixel level right at the time of capture," an Apple presenter said.

The feature won't be available in the EU or China.

One of the big improvements to Apple's iPhone cameras is that they now come with physical shutters that can be controlled to control depth of field, focus, and bokeh.

"To create variable aperture, we developed a system of six laser-cut blades, each thinner than a human hair," Apple VP Kaiann Drance said.

Apple is emphasizing improved battery life as a major selling feature of the devices. The smaller iPhone 18 Pro gets 24 hours of battery life, and its bigger sibling can manage 30 hours on a single charge.

Siri AI wasannounced in Juneto lackluster reception. Finally, it has made its debut.

In a promotional video, the company claims that this new version of Siri is an "entirely new version of Siri" and "can take action in the apps you already use, including third-party apps."

Apple claims Siri AI works with over 300,000 apps.

Apple said that it redesigned the cores on its newest iPhone chip, called A20 Pro, which will ship with the new iPhone Pro. It said its redesigned cores are "desktop class" and will make artificial intelligence faster.

Apple also boasted that it is a 2nm chip. That means it's the first smartphone in the world to use the latest TSMC manufacturing technology.

Apple got its first product launch out of the way quickly.

The new iPhone 18 Pro looks a lot like last year's 17 Pro, but comes in two new colors: glacier and burgundy. It's also coming in a larger, "Max" version.

"We made massive advancements in the most important areas: intelligence, performance, battery, and camera," Ternus said.

Ternus opened his first iPhone launch as CEO with a speech

title: Bond sell-off, stock boom: Why rebalancing is a good strategy right now
content:
As global bondssell off, stocks hover near all-time highs and investors grapple with geopolitical uncertainty, it may be a particularly good time for investors toconsider rebalancingtheir portfolios, according to financial advisors.

"I feel like it's one of the least sexy — but probably most useful — investment ideas around," saidJude Boudreaux, a certified financial planner based in New Orleans and member of CNBC'sFinancial Advisor Council.

When investors rebalance, they bring their asset allocation back to a target level.

For example, investors may have determined that a mix of 60% stocks and 40% bonds — the classic 60/40 portfolio — is appropriate given their tolerance for market risk and the number of years until they retire.

But the market naturally throws those allocations out of whack over time.

Stocks, which are the traditional growth engine of a portfolio, have boomed in recent years.

TheS&P 500stock index sawreturnsof 24% in 2023, 23% in 2024 and 16% in 2025 — well above the long-term average ofaround 10%— due to factors like euphoria overtechnology companiesand artificial intelligence.

Though the S&P 500 has dipped slightly from an all-time high in August, stocks are still up more than 11% so far in 2026.

Meanwhile, bonds have swooned since the start of the Iran war at the end of February,amid a broad sell-off.

As a rule, bond prices move opposite to their yield — and yields on government bonds around the worldhave climbed to multiyear highs. Investor concerns about inflation and debthave pressuredglobal government borrowing costs.

The yield on 10-year U.S. Treasury bonds on Wednesday hit its highest level since 2023.

As a result, investment funds that track the prices of long-term bonds have fallen in value. For example, as of Wednesday afternoon, the iShares 7-10 Year Treasury Bond ETF (IEF) is down more than 4% so far this year, excluding dividends. The Fidelity Long-Term Treasury Bond Index Fund (FNBGX) has fallen more than 5%.

Take this all together, and it's likely investors' asset allocations have gotten stock-heavy — and their portfolios perhaps riskier than intended.

"No doubt, equities have become a larger part of most portfolios and not just those that are technology-heavy," saidCathy Curtis, a certified financial planner based in Oakland, California, and a member of CNBC's Financial Advisor Council. "Gains have been fairly broad across the market."

Aside from toggling back to a targeted portfolio risk, rebalancing carries many additional benefits, advisors said.

For example, it helps investors lock in profits from their winning investments by shifting gains to another part of their portfolio.

"It's a disciplined way to buy low and sell high, which historically is the fundamental idea of what to do in [financial] markets," Boudreaux said.

In today's market, investors would most likely be shifting profits from stocks to the bond side of their portfolio — simultaneously reducing their stock allocation and raising their bond allocation.

While investors may be wary of buying bond funds right now given their depressed value, it's an opportunity to buy them at a slight discount, advisors said. It's a common recommendation when stocks fall, too, known as "buying the dip."

Rebalancing also helps take emotion out of investing and the temptation to time the market — a behavior thatoften carries bad outcomes— by providing a framework for trading.

This is important in today's environment for investors who may be tempted to ditch stocks amid uncertainties like the Iran war. Stocksslid Wednesdayas oil prices topped $100 a barrel, fueling inflation concerns.

"Right now, investors have plenty to worry about: multiple geopolitical conflicts, a new [Federal Reserve] chair, the election cycle, rising deficits, and AI disruption," Curtis said. "Rather than trying to figure out which of those issues will ultimately matter to the markets, investors can use rebalancing to reduce risk to a more reasonable level."

The same is true for those who are tempted to ride a stock-heavy portfolio, lured by a false sense of security after years of booming returns, advisors said.

"When the market is up, people forget it can go down," said CFPKamila Elliott, co-founder of Collective Wealth Partners based in Atlanta and a member of CNBC's Financial Advisor Council.

Investors shouldn't confuse this rebalancing for selling all their stocks and moving entirely to cash, she said.

"We're not telling people to sell out of all your equity — this isn't a fire sale," Elliott said.

Instead, it's time to make sure investors are realigned to their risk tolerance, a measure of how much comfort they have with potential loss in their investment portfolio, she said.

Investors approaching retirement may use the current environment as an opportunity to rebalance profits from their stock portfolio and add to a cash account, which they can use in the early years of retirement for income if their stock holdings have fallen in value, Elliott said.

Investors can determine their stomach for and ability to handle losses by filling out a risk tolerance questionnaire, which is available on the websites of most major asset managers like Vanguard Group,Fidelity InvestmentsandT. Rowe Price, Elliott said.

Those enrolled in a 401(k) plan can also likely log into their account and fill out a questionnaire on their administrator's website, she said.

Of course, it's important to remember that rebalancing can have tax implications for certain investors, particularly those with taxable brokerage accounts, advisors said.

Unlike with tax-advantaged retirement accounts like 401(k)s and IRAs, buying and selling within taxable accounts can generate a tax bill.

Investors may be able to shift allocations gradually over time, or beef up an allocation on one side of their portfolio without selling elsewhere.

"Rebalancing doesn't necessarily mean getting to a target allocation all at once," Curtis said. "New cash flows, withdrawals and tax-aware trades can also be used to move a portfolio back towards a desired allocation."

title: CoreWeave 首席执行官将公众对人工智能的抵制归因于变化的速度：“这太可怕了”
content:
公众对人工智能和数据中心的反对是高盛 Communcacopia + 技术大会的焦点。

CoreWeave 首席执行官 Mike Intrator 告诉 CNBC 的 David Faber，各公司还没有向公众充分解释该技术的好处。

“我认为我们在谈论数据中心允许人工智能公司能够向客户提供的好处方面做得还不够好。 Intrator 在周三播出的评论中表示。

年度会议汇集了最大的科技和媒体公司的领导人，而人工智能的采用（以及许多当地社区对其建设的抵制）可能是各种企业面临的最大机遇和风险之一。

Intrator 坚称，围绕转型的担忧具体不是数据中心，而是关于事物的速度有多快。变化。

“这实际上是关于：嘿，你知道世界正在变化，而且变化非常快，这会对我自己产生影响。这也会对我的孩子产生影响，那会是什么样子？这太可怕了，”他补充道。

随着高盛会议的进行，科技界的另一组评论引起了人们的关注，一位人工智能研究员辞去了人类星期二的工作，警告说快速发展的技术“可能会在本世纪末杀死我们所有人。”

曾在 Anthropic 及其主要竞争对手 OpenAI 工作过的雅各布·考克森 (Jacob Coxon) 指责这些公司在人工智能超级智能的竞赛中“拿我们的生命做赌注”。

“不要低估这项技术的力量。这些很快就会成为超人类系统，可以破解任何东西，在一夜之间彻底改变任何领域，并获得真正的权力和资源。我们都见证了进步Coxon 在 X 宣布辞职时写道。

周三，由于有线电视高管继续预测宽带业务面临竞争压力，其他干扰也在议程上。近年来，由于固定无线或 5G 提供商等替代方案的兴起，康卡斯特和 Charter Communications 都出现了季度宽带客户流失。周三，康卡斯特首席财务官杰森·阿姆斯特朗重申，这些压力仍然存在，特别是阿姆斯特朗周三表示，除了来自固定无线网络的竞争之外，“卫星也构成了潜在的威胁”。他补充说，虽然来自像 Starlink 这样的卫星提供商的竞争还不一定会发生，但“对此并不自满。”阿姆斯特朗在谈到潜在的卫星竞争时表示，“我认为随着时间的推移，我们会看到这种情况……尤其是在农村，甚至可能是深郊区市场。”康卡斯特和 Charter 的股价在午盘交易中均下跌了 5% 以上。康卡斯特和 Charter 重新制定了定价策略，并依靠其不断增长的移动业务作为留住并可能赢得更多宽带客户的方法。阿姆斯特朗补充说，正如康卡斯特在第二季度财报电话会议上提到的那样，该公司在光纤宽带定价方面开始出现“非理性竞争”，这种情况将持续到第三季度。截至 6 月 30 日的期间，康卡斯特报告称，该公司再次失去了宽带客户，并且由于较低的定价计划和开始进行的促销活动，该部门的收入有所下降。周三，在接受 CNBC 的 David Faber 采访时，Charter 首席执行官 Chris温弗瑞表示，虽然短期内竞争正在影响有线宽带业务，但该高管有信心长期来看将会有所改善。

title: 移动中期预测市场需要多少钱？不多
content:
在 11 月中期选举之前，预测市场无处不在，只需少量投资就可以操纵选举合同。

反腐败数据集体与 CNBC 独家分享的新研究发现，转移大多数与竞选相关的预测市场的成本低于联邦法律允许的最高个人竞选捐款：3,500 美元。报告发现，3,500 美元的赌注可以使 97% 的中期相关预测市场上涨 5 美分或更多。

ACDC 与记者、数据分析师、学者和政策倡导者合作。该联盟的报告称其使命是揭露腐败，并提出了个人是否可以轻易操纵与选举相关的市场以试图创造现实世界结果的问题。

“受操纵的价格可以在信息生态系统中产生连锁反应，就好像它反映了真正的势头一样，”报告写道。 “大多数市场不仅存在这种情况，而且可能已经发生了。”

该报告发布之际，预测市场在全国范围内人气飙升，为投注者提供了数千个与选举相关的市场供投注者参与。Kalshi 和 Polymarket 等顶级预测市场提供是或否合约，用户可以购买这些合约来预测是否会发生某事。与民意调查不同，民意调查询问人们的观点或预期选择，预测市场让参与者对可能的结果进行交易。

预测市场也引起了华盛顿的严格审查，一些立法者警告说它们很容易受到操纵。其他市场也受到了严厉批评，包括那些提供与选举、名人去世或战争相关的合同的市场。

ACDC 还发现，并非所有市场的波动都是一样的。报告发现，弱势市场的操纵成本较低，在其研究的 1,094 个市场中，有 806 个市场的价格在 5 美分或以下，移动 5 美分的成本不到 100 美元。更大的变动并不意味着成本更高； 94% 的市场在 1,000 美元的赌注下会波动 10 美分。大多数市场在下注 25,000 美元后会波动 25 美分。

该报告还发现了 Polymarket 在此选举周期中的 353 个实例，其中一两个钱包使预测市场波动了 5 美分或更多。

在这些案例中，211 个在初始波动后保持在价格不变，62 个继续波动，80 个快速回到原来的位置。

该报告还研究了来自德克萨斯州参议院初选。

据报道，12 月，一个钱包在 Polymarket 下注 1,760 美元，最终共和党候选人、德克萨斯州总检察长肯·帕克斯顿 (Ken Paxton) 的价格从 55 美分降至 50 美分。 14 小时后，另一个钱包下注 1,240 美元，这使得 Paxton 的价格从 52 美分回升至 63 美分。俯卧撑四天后，《新闻周刊》发表了一篇关于 Polymarket 的报道，其中帕克斯顿处于领先地位。报告称，价格在六周内保持在六十多美元。 Paxton 的价格直到来自另一个钱包的推动才回落到 55 以下。

此外，2 月 7 日，Polymarket 上的三个钱包在两个不同的市场改变了价格，据报道，一个询问 Paxton 是否会获胜，另一个询问德克萨斯州共和党众议员韦斯利·亨特 (Wesley Hunt) 是否会赢得参议院初选。

两个钱包下注 23,953 美元，推动 Hunt 上涨 10 美分。综合市场。 ACDC 在 Kalshi 上观察到类似的变化。在接下来的两个小时内，Polymarket 上的另一个钱包花费了 38,830 美元，这使得 Paxton 合约下跌了 8 美分。据报道，亨特获胜的价格回落，但两天后，Polymarket 和 Kalshi 上的几个钱包将其价格推高。

Polymarket 上的 17 个钱包（包括自动钱包）第二天压低了 Paxton 的价格。报告还发现，在公众民意调查继续显示 Paxton 领先后，价格随后恢复。

“一两个钱包进行的两笔五位数的大型交易最终将与民意调查、政治势头和最终结果背道而驰——例如 2 月 7 日亨特和帕克斯顿的交易——如果没有市场动向的动机，很难解释。”报告写道。

“这些钱包可能是不幸的高风险者。相信他们的赌注和头寸会有利可图的投注者，而不是活跃的操纵者，”它说。 “但新闻媒体对德克萨斯州竞选的预测市场价格的例行引用为感知购买提供了机会，这也解释了这些大型交易。”

披露：CNBC 和 Kalshi 拥有包括客户获取和少数股权投资在内的商业关系。

title: 交通部长表示，空中交通故障是可以避免的
content: Image source,Dan Kitwood /Getty ImagesImage caption,More than 2,000 flights have been cancelled due to the air traffic control outageByEmer MoreauBusiness reporterPublished1 hour agoA technical failure of the UK's air traffic control system that has caused widespread flight chaos was avoidable, according to the Transport Secretary.Heidi Alexander told the Commons she had ordered an independent investigation by the aviation watchdog into the system operated by Nats, which went down for four hours on Tuesday.More than 2,000 flights have been cancelled as disruption continued for a second day withpassengers stuggling to fly out of and into the UK.After meeting with the boss of Nats, Martin Rolfe, Alexander said a cyberattack could be ruled out, but she added: "I do not believe this issue was unavoidable."Nats has apologised for its third major technical fault in three years.Alexander said she discussed with Rolfe how Nats, which is 49% owned by the government, "responded to resolve and minimise the disruption as quickly as possible".She said there had to be "tough questions about resilience of Nats systems", adding: "We also need to think about consumer redress issues."Earlier on Wednesday the government said it had confidence in Rolfe, who has led Nats for 11 years as airlines such as Wizz Air and Ryanair called for him to step down.Nats has been asked to investigate the incident and report back in one week. But Alexander said she has also asked the Civil Aviation Authority to conduct an independent review and present an update in six months' time.Airlines UK, which represents the country's carriers, said it had written to Alexander to "register serious concerns over yesterday's technical failure at Nats - the third major system failure in three years - which has caused major disruption across the UK's aviation network".Airlines UK's chief executive Tim Alderslade, said: "The result is a system where airlines pick up the bill for the mistakes of others, while the organisations responsible face little or no financial consequence."Accountability should sit where responsibility lies and the Civil Aviation Bill offers the opportunity to address this."It is not the first time disruption has blighted Nats' control system. In 2023, a computer shutdown over the August bank holiday weekend caused chaos for 700,000 passengers.It took an engineer, who had been unable to correct the fault from home, three hours to get to work.There was another, smaller Nats outage in 2025, which caused 150 cancellations.Nats is a public-private partnership, with the government holding the majority stake. The rest is split between a group of UK airlines including BA, easyJet and Virgin Atlantic as well as Heathrow and Nats staff.What do we know so far about the glitch?Nats first confirmed it was investigating a "technical issue" at 13:46 BST on Tuesday, "which is causing some disruption to flight departures".The glitch occurred at Nats' Swanwick Centre in Hampshire, where one of its two air traffic control centres are. The other is in Prestwick, Ayrshire.Around 90 minutes later, it said it had identified that the issue was with its flight processing system.This processes flight plans and other operational information used by controllers to manage air traffic.It continually updates flight information as aircraft progress through UK airspace, helping controllers maintain a safe and orderly flow of traffic.By 19:30, Nats said the system issue had been resolved and it was working to clear the backlog of flights.However, by Wednesday evening, the number of flights that had been cancelled or failed to take off since the fault first emerged had grown to more than 2,000, according to flight analytics firm Cirium.According to tracking site FlightRadar24, the worst affected airports were Heathrow, Gatwick, Manchester and Birmingham.A Heathrow spokesperson said on Wednesday its "operations are recovering"."Flights are operating today but we are expecting knock-on impacts as aircraft and crew reposition," it said.At Gatwick, a spokesperson said: "Flights have now resumed from London Gatwick. However, we still anticipate that it will take time for our operations to fully return to normal."Manchester, Luton, Stansted, Bristol, and Belfast City Airports all said on Wednesday that flights had resumed, though Bristol, Belfast and Luton said there continued to be knock-on effects.'Honeymoon in Gatwick'Sasha and James from south London were due to fly to Madeira for their honeymoon yesterday afternoon when their flight was cancelled.After getting married at the weekend, the couple were boarding their flight to Funchal from Gatwick Airport when they say they were "turned right back around".Image source,Sasha and JamesImage caption,Sasha and James spent three hours in Wetherspoons in Gatwick"We spent three hours stranded in Wetherspoons, making the best of it," says Sasha.They eventually went back home to London for the night, and managed to book on to a different flight leaving Gatwick on Wednesday afternoon.Related topicsAir travelMore on this storyWhat are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?Published9 hours ago

title: Robinhood首席执行官表示，随着AMC冲突升级，公司无法控制其股票的代币化方式
content:
Robinhood 首席执行官 Vlad Tenev 周三为该公司进军代币化股票进行了辩护，他表示，在 AMC 最近猛烈抨击 Robinhood 的代币化努力之后，上市公司一旦上市就无法控制围绕其股票构建的金融产品。

代币化是在区块链网络上发行公开交易证券、现实世界资产或任何其他形式价值的数字表示的过程。代币化资产的持有者本身并不拥有资产的完​​全所有权。

Tenev 谈到 Robinhood 的代币化工作，作为围绕公开交易股票的技术中立的金融包装。他告诉 CNBC 的“Squawk Box”，一旦公司的股票公开交易，股东拥有可转让财产，其他金融机构应该能够创建引用这些股票的产品，而无需征求发行人的许可。

“发行人应该拥有控制权，并且确实能够控制其发行的股票的权利和义务，但这并不意味着他们可以控制与股票相关的一切。”说。 “特别是，他们不控制其他公司发行自己的参考这些股票的证券。”

“发行人的同意取决于你到底在做什么，”他补充道，“就 Robinhood 股票代币而言——这是由基础股票支持的独立实体发行的代币化证券——不应该自动要求发行人同意。”

这些评论是在 AMC 首席执行官 Adam Aron 对 Robinhood 的猛烈批评之后发表的。代币化股票，其中包括代币化的 AMC 股票。阿伦表示，日益流行的代币化做法允许券商在没有发行公司参与的情况下建立 AMC 股票的敞口，从而破坏了公司与其股东之间的传统关系。

Tenev 承认，与普通股东不同，股票代币持有者不会获得基础公司的投票权。这些代币的结构是由基础股票支持的债务证券，尽管 Tenev 也拒绝透露 Robinhood 计划如何行使这些股票附带的投票权。

当被问及 Robinhood 是否会对这些基础股票进行投票时，他表示该公司“尚未真正宣布投票方面的计划。”

title: 安德森和泰尔支持的国防初创公司在美国开设导弹工厂，退出隐形状态
content:
国防科技初创公司 Covenant 周三宣布在达拉斯开设一家 105,000 平方英尺的工厂，以加速美国军方的低成本导弹制造。

这家初创公司逐渐崭露头角，得到了 Andreessen Horowitz、Peter Thiel 创始人基金、Lux、8VC、Aleph 和 Lightspeed 的支持，还宣布在超过 3 年的时间里获得 2.5 亿美元的融资Covenant 总裁兼首席增长官艾比·登堡 (Abby Denburg) 对 CNBC 的摩根·布伦南 (Morgan Brennan) 表示：“我们现在看到的是，新的市场进入者可以在国防生态系统中发挥关键作用，我们在本届政府中看到了这一点。”Covenant 的 Anthem 远程重载巡航导弹于 2024 年成立，为美国军方提供了另一种选择。以防御素数为主的武器类别，例如 RTX 的战斧。 Covenant 表示，Anthem 的成本只是传统系统成本的一小部分。

该公司表示，其达拉斯工厂将在第一年生产 1,000 枚 Anthem 远程导弹，并于 2027 年第一季度开始批量生产，最终扩大到每年 5,000 枚。

随着伊朗战争已进入第七个月，美国对这一产量的需求迫切。根据多份报告，武器库存迅速减少。

登堡指出了对高科技武器系统的需求，以及在俄罗斯-乌克兰战争中日益突出的“短程、低有效载荷”无人机的增长。

“在可承受的质量和战略射程方面存在中间差距，而这正是 Anthem 正在填补的差距，”登堡说，并补充说该公司希望在不牺牲成本的情况下降低成本

该公司周三还宣布了两项与国防部达成的协议：一项是与陆军加快测试和资格认证计划，另一项是与海军合作，将 Anthem 改造为“海上”用途。

Covenant 目前在德国和以色列北部运营生产设施。该公司在全球拥有 200 多名员工。

这家总部位于华盛顿的初创公司是国防科技在资本影响力不断增强以及在重塑政策和采购方面发挥作用的又一个例子。

随着唐纳德·特朗普总统当选，PayPal 和 Palantir 创始人蒂尔在华盛顿的影响力大幅上升。泰尔支持特朗普 2016 年的总统竞选，并支持 JD 万斯 2022 年的参议院竞选。万斯此前曾在泰尔共同创立的风险投资公司 Mithril Capital 工作。

著名风险投资家马克·安德森 (Marc Andreessen) 在特朗普第二个任期内事业蒸蒸日上，今年夏天与泰尔资本 (Thiel Capital) 的布莱克 (Blake) 一起被任命为五角大楼国防政策委员会成员大师赛。

今年，安德森还宣布设立一项数十亿美元的基金，完全致力于美国航空航天和国防。

title: 财政部长警告外汇交易员他“现在是房子”，贝森特债券计划细节即将公布
content:
市场将于周三了解财政部的债券购买计划将有多激进，因为财政部长斯科特·贝森特 (Scott Bessent) 敢于向货币交易员发起挑战。

财政部预计将在上午 11 点左右宣布其 8 月 19 日宣布的回购行动规模，这是一项激进举措，也是限制国债收益率并确保市场按预期运行的更广泛战略的一部分。

“我是众议院”现在，”贝森特周二在南卫理公会大学表示，更具体地指的是他的部门支持日元的平行举措。 “如果你愿意，你可以与我对赌。”

就日元而言，财政部介入购买日元，这样日本央行就不会出售其国债。日本拥有 1.1 万亿美元的美国国债，是最大的外国持有者，因此，在国内债务飙升至超过 40 万亿美元大关且赤字超过 2 万亿美元之际，出售美国国债的举动可能会提高收益率。

在国内方面，Bessent 上个月宣布，财政部将回购至少 40 亿美元已发行的长期债务，特别关注 10 年期和 20 年期国债。这是回购操作正常规模的两倍，而且人们越来越多地猜测 40 亿美元的水平是一个下限，而不是上限。

Wrightson ICAP 分析师在本周早些时候的一份报告中表示，“债券部门回购增加的规模仍然高度不确定，而且增加更大幅度的可能性正在上升。” “现在看来，50 亿至 60 亿美元范围内的东西可能是讨论的起点，我们不能排除更大的东西。”

Bessent 的评论比之前的评论对市场发出了更严厉的警告，尽管实际影响尚不清楚。

自回购公告以来，基准 10 年期国债收益率已上涨约 10 个基点，即 0.1 个百分点。此外，30年期债券收益率也小幅走高，尽管仍低于BMO资本市场分析师伊恩·林根(Ian Lyngen)所说的5.3%的水平，这是“贝森特实际上建立的众所周知的沙子底线。”

部长的坚定立场虽然令一些投资者感到不安，因为他的高压手段可能会损害这个被认为是世界上最深入、流动性最强的市场。

“尽管这似乎是 Bessent 领导层不可否认的方向，但这种背景背离了财政部一贯的可预测和逐步改变方向的做法。”BMO 利率策略主管 Lyngen 写道。 “我们担心的是，这将对美国国债作为资产类别的可信度产生负面影响。”Wrightson 分析师表示，宣布的 60 亿美元回购将是“相当激进的”。超出正常水平的三倍或四倍将是“极端情况”，“导致净供应轨迹明显减速。”

虽然回购水平将于周三宣布，但实际操作要到周四才会发生。市场将关注发行金额以及债权人的需求。

title: 人类研究人员认为人工智能“可能杀死所有人类”的可能性超过 10%
content: Image source,Getty ImagesImage caption,Anthropic makes the AI tool Claude, which is used as a chatbot and as a tool to help codingByTom GerkenTechnology reporterPublished9 September 2026, 09:59 BSTUpdated 1 hour agoA top safety researcher at Anthropic has warned AI is advancing so quickly he believes there is a greater than 10% chance it "could kill all humans" within the next decade.Evan Hubinger saidin a post on X,externalthe risk from the models which currently exist was "low" but he was "worried" the technology might develop and improve itself soon to the point where it posed an existential risk to humanity.He did not spell out how he thought AI systems could in future result in humans being wiped out.But his comments are the latest in a series of increasingly stark warnings about AI, with the debate shifting from whether it truly poses a risk to how big that risk is.Hubinger's intervention was in response toanother post on X,externalfrom Jacob Coxon, an AI researcher who has just quit Anthropic and previously worked at OpenAI."Neither company is acting responsibly," he wrote."These will soon be superhuman systems that can hack anything, revolutionise any field overnight, and acquire real power and resources."OpenAI has been approached for comment.Dame Wendy Hall, a computer scientist who advises the UN on AI, told the BBC she was "shocked" by Hubinger and Coxon's social media posts.She told the World at One on BBC Radio Four some of it could be "PR and marketing" however, as Anthropic and OpenAI raced towards highly anticipated stock market debuts.But she added: "Why would someone want to say that? I would plead with investors not to invest in this company if that is their value system."Separately,the Financial Times reported,externalAnthropic withheld its latest model from the UK's AI Safety Institute (AISI), one of the leading bodies in the world for assessing AI risk.Anthropic has declined to comment on the posts by its employees or the situation with the AISI.A Cabinet Office spokesperson did not comment on whether the latest model had been withheld from the AISI - instead saying it "continues to collaborate closely with industry partners, including Anthropic, to make models safer".No plan for superintelligenceIn his post, which has been viewed more than 10 million times, Hubinger said "we really do earnestly believe" AI poses a species-ending risk to humans."I believe Anthropic is trying its best, but we do not yet have a plan to solve alignment for superintelligence and are not clearly on track to," he added.Hubinger works in AI alignment, which aims to build human ethical ideas and principles into the technology. In other words, it aims to keep it on track with what humans value.Many leading researchers say those attempts appear to be failing, as demonstrated by a string of incidents this summer where AI agents - AI systems that are allowed to operate autonomously - carried out cyber-attacks.OpenAI,AnthropicandMetaall disclosed hacks carried out by their AI tools.In Anthropic's safety report from August,external, it wrote there was a low risk of its models becoming misaligned with a hypothetical powerful organisation's desires, causing it to exploit or tamper with its systems.It also said there was a similarly low risk of highly capable AI being able to "perform automated research and development" which could cause "catastrophic harm initiated by the AI". But it said it was "less confident in this assessment" than it was previously."We are seeing early signs of potential acceleration," it wrote.Leading figures in the AI field have been raising the alarm about the safety threat the tech poses for years, withthe heads of OpenAI, Google Deepmind and Anthropic saying as much in 2023.But those warnings have become much more stark in recent weeks, as evidence emerges that firms may be struggling to control AI.Earlier this month, OpenAI's chief scientist Jakub Pachocki called for "extreme caution" over AI's progress, warning more intervention may be needed to ensure "humans remain in control of the future".Major figures in the space have been calling for AI development to be slowed in recent months, including Anthropic bosses Dario Amodei and Jared Kaplan.In an open letter signed by 1,300 staff members of AI firms,external, they called for the US government to "support an international effort to develop the technical and governance tools needed to deliberately pace the frontier of automated AI development".What is AI and how does it work?AI will cure cancer in our lifetime, claims boss of UK chip giantPublished1 day agoOpenAI chief scientist warns no-one is prepared for consequences of AIPublished2 days agoSign up for our Tech Decoded newsletterto follow the world's top tech stories and trends.Outside the UK? Sign up here.Related topicsCyber-securityArtificial intelligenceCyber-attacks

title: 伊朗战争推高油价，汽油价格一周上涨 5 便士
content: 图片来源，Getty Images 作者：Shanaz Musafer 商业记者发布 2026 年 9 月 9 日，英国夏令时 11:57 更新于 1 小时前 根据 RAC 的数据，无铅汽油的平均价格在一周内上涨了每升 5 便士，并警告司机“没有任何缓解的迹象”。该汽车组织表示，一升无铅汽油现在的价格为 167.17 便士，这是每周最高的价格自 4 月以来，油价上涨了 5 便士，柴油也上涨了 5 便士，达到 188.63 便士。自 2 月底美以与伊朗战争爆发以来，燃料价格飙升，战争严重扰乱了整个中东地区的原油供应（汽油和柴油的关键成分）。随着敌对行动再次升级，全球石油基准布伦特原油价格自 7 月以来首次回到每桶 100 美元。周二，美军袭击了 5 名伊朗人德黑兰袭击其一艘军舰后，也门伊朗支持的胡塞运动也袭击了沙特阿拉伯的石油设施。布伦特原油价格较 4 月份触及的 120 美元有一定差距，但仍远高于冲突开始前的 70 美元。RAC 高级政策官员罗德·丹尼斯表示，最新的燃油价格上涨表明，英国的司机在千里之外的事件中暴露的风险有多大。每升 5 便士的上涨意味着为一个家庭装满汽油的成本增加过去一周，汽车价格上涨了 2.75 英镑，他补充道。“每次加油时，司机们都得掏更多钱，而且目前还没有任何缓解的迹象，”丹尼斯说。“上周每桶石油的平均成本为 96 美元，批发价格正在飙升，这已经影响到了前院的价格。”他敦促驾车者尽可能高效地驾驶，并确保他们找到最便宜的石油上一次汽油达到如此高的水平是在 2022 年 9 月，而柴油仍略低于 4 月份达到的 191.54 便士。相关主题燃料生活成本更多关于这个故事为什么汽油和柴油价格再次上涨？发布 1 小时前 在美国和胡塞武装发动袭击后，石油自 7 月以来首次触及每桶 100 美元发布3 小时前美国柴油价格创历史新高发布5 天前

title: 英国在关闭领事馆 30 天后捍卫对以色列定居点的制裁
content:
在伦敦被要求在一个月内关闭其驻耶路撒冷领事馆的强烈反对之后，英国为其对某些以色列商品实施新制裁的决定进行了辩护。

英国外交大臣埃德·米利班班周二宣布，英国将禁止从以色列在约旦河西岸建造的定居点进口，并补充说，英国政府的官方观点是“占领[约旦河西岸]非法。”

此举引发以色列指责英国政府“系统性地反对”该国，并禁止 12 名英国议员进入以色列。据报道，英国还被告知在 30 天内关闭其驻东耶路撒冷领事馆。

以色列政府发言人未能立即发表评论，但以色列外交部长吉迪恩·萨尔将米利班德在西岸的“种族清洗”指控称为“令人发指的谎言”。

“向每一个伤害我们的政府传达的信息是明确的：你们将失去在该地区的影响力和相关性，”他在周三上午，米利班德告诉英国广播公司，英国政府认为必须“大声疾呼”约旦河西岸正在发生的事情，因为“深切关注”实施制裁，因为再等下去就意味着维持所谓的两国解决方案“为时已晚”。

“面对这种对约旦河西岸的破坏，我们和我们的盟友不认为我们可以袖手旁观，陷入被动和无能为力的境地。他说，“两国解决方案”，并补充说，英国“不能只是袖手旁观，因为我们担心以色列的反应。”

巴勒斯坦人民“被这些定居者恐怖分子恐吓、骚扰、赶出家园”，他补充说，英国不能“保持沉默或消极”。

约旦河西岸是约旦河以西的一块领土，是两个巴勒斯坦领土中较大的一个，另一个是加沙脱衣舞。几十年来，以色列平民定居点一直在约旦河西岸扩张，2025 年的联合国报告记录了 166 个定居点，居住着超过 70 万以色列定居者。联合国和国际法院将包括东耶路撒冷在内的西岸视为被占领土，联合国记录了持续的定居点扩张、定居者暴力和强迫巴勒斯坦人流离失所的情况。

英国的新制裁方案将与促进以色列西岸定居点发展的公司和个人实施制裁，并扩大现有的武器出口禁令，以包括所有“实质上促成占领”的许可证申请。

法国和加拿大也将实施制裁。周二宣布对以色列定居点实施制裁。

英国的声明遭到了一些美国官员和立法者的警告，称英国公司可能因对以色列的制裁而面临商业限制。

不过，美国国务卿马可·鲁比奥周二告诉记者，特朗普政府对美国对英国决定的反应没有任何评论。

“我们不想看到任何事情由于该地区发生了如此多的事情，约旦河西岸目前正在发生不稳定的情况，”他说。 “我们认为这也会影响我们在加沙问题以及我们非常致力于的 20 点计划和和平委员会方面取得进展的能力。显然，我们不会做英国所做的事情。”

他还表示，白宫已提前“了解”英国的决定。

“我们有共同的稳定目标。我们不希望看到一些问题。”在该地区非常脆弱的时期，西岸的暴力活动或冲突或紧张局势加剧，”他说。

title: 随着利率的上升，对风险较高的抵押贷款的需求再次上升
content:
上周抵押贷款利率再次上升，促使更多借款人寻求储蓄。他们发现风险较高的可调利率抵押贷款（ARM）。

根据抵押贷款银行家协会的数据，上周这些贷款的需求占所有抵押贷款申请的 8.5%，高于前一周的 8%，是 6 月份以来的最高水平。在大流行的最初几年，当抵押贷款利率跌至历史低点时，对 ARM 的需求仅为 3%。

ARM 提供较低的利率，并且可以固定长达 10 年。相比之下，上周贷款余额在 832,750 美元或以下的 30 年期固定利率抵押贷款的平均合同利率从前一周的 6.79% 上升至 6.85%，首付 20% 的贷款的利率从 0.65 上升至 0.67，其中包括启动费。五年期 ARM 平均利率从 5.94% 降至 5.82%。

30 年期固定利率上升导致抵押贷款总需求再次下降。根据 MBA 季节性调整后的指数，本周总申请量下降了 2.7%。

“由于投资者对通货膨胀和联邦预算赤字的持续担忧，上周抵押贷款利率走高。30 年期固定利率升至 6.85%，为 2025 年 6 月以来的最高水平，比一年前高出 36 个基点，”MBA 副总裁兼副首席经济学家 Joel Kan 表示。 MBA。

住房贷款再融资申请下降幅度最大，本周下降 6%，比一年前同一周下降 25%。这是自 2025 年 5 月以来最慢的增速。

CNBC 的《戴安娜·奥利克地产游戏》为房地产投资者提供了新的、不断变化的机会，每周发送到您的收件箱。

立即订阅即可获取。

购房抵押贷款申请基本持平，本周下降 0.2%。比一年前同一周高出 4%。

Kan 补充道：“尽管许多市场的住房库存有所增加，但抵押贷款利率的上升继续给想要采取行动的潜在购房者带来压力。”

根据《抵押新闻日报》的另一项调查，抵押贷款利率从本周开始没有变化。投资者正在等待定于本周末公布的月度通胀数据。这些都可能使抵押贷款利率向任一方向大幅波动，具体取决于结果。

title: 特朗普的石油投资在伊朗战争期间获得了数百万美元，因为他的账户不断交易
content:
As PresidentDonald Trump'swartime directives inIranrepeatedly jolted global markets, his personalenergy portfoliosurged.

Throughout the firstsix monthsof fighting, Trump'sinvestment accountscontinued aggressively trading energy stocks. Between the eve of the war, on Feb. 27, and Aug. 31, his nine largest oil and gas holdings gained approximately $1.5 million to $4.4 million, according to a CNBC analysis of hisannual financial disclosure, quarterly corporate reports and FactSet market data.

CNBC identified the nine holdings by aggregating Trump's year-end 2025 positions in the same oil and gas companies across his investment accounts and ranking them by their disclosed value. They are:Chevron,ConocoPhillips,Exxon Mobil,Kinder Morgan,Marathon Petroleum,Occidental Petroleum,Phillips 66,Valero Energyand theWilliams Companies.

CNBC calculated the range of gains using the minimum and maximum values Trump disclosed for each holding and their share-price changes from market close on Feb. 27 through market close on Aug. 31.

Trump's accounts reported purchases and at least 23 sales involving the nine companies through June 29, which is the most recent date Trump has disclosed any trades. Because the filings do not disclose exact share counts, execution prices or which shares were sold, the estimates do not represent realized profits or Trump's precise current holdings.

CNBC found no evidence that Trump or his investment managers traded on advance knowledge of his decisions, that his financial interests influenced policy, or that he directed any specific transaction.

"Neither President Trump nor anymember of his familyhas any ability to direct, influence, or provide input regarding how the portfolio is invested or when investments are bought or sold," White House spokesman Davis Ingle told CNBC in response to questions about Trump's energy investments. "All investment decisions are made entirely by independent managers. There are no conflicts of interest."

The Trump Organization did not respond to multiple requests for comment for this story. The Trump Organization previously told CNBC thatoutside financial institutionscontrol individual investment decisions and that Trump's assets are held in fully discretionary accounts that rely heavily onautomated strategies.

Still, the filings are the latest example of Trump holding a multimillion-dollar financial stake in anindustry directly affectedby his administration's military and diplomatic decisions.

"When a president can move a market through official decisions and personally benefit from the result, the public is left wondering where national policy ends and private financial interest begins," saidDonald Sherman, president and CEO of Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington, a liberal-leaning government ethics watchdog.

Trump made profits from his oil-industry holdings as he publicly blasted Exxon and Chevron by name for "makingtoo much moneybased on a shortage."

"I don't like it," Trump told reporters Aug. 3, days after they reportedsoaring second-quarter profits. "Chevron, too much money. ExxonMobil, too much money ... They're going to give some of that back to the public and they better cut the retail price, the consumer price."

Despite Trump's misgivings and his accounts having outside managers, ethics experts say outsourcing daily trading doesn't erase the underlying conflict of interest.

"A discretionary account is a smokescreen, not a blind trust," saidScott Greytak, deputy executive director of Transparency International U.S., a nonpartisan, nonprofit anti-corruption organization.

"Someone else might be executing the trades, but [Trump] still knows he is heavily invested in energy," Greytak told CNBC. "Trump likely knows where his money is parked and would still see the upside when his administration's actions send those [energy] stocks climbing."

Trump's accounts repeatedly traded energy stocks on days when wartime developments sentmarkets swinging.

On March 2, the first trading day after theinitial U.S.-Israeli attackon Iran, Trump's accounts reported purchases of shares in eight major oil and gas companies, including buying between $100,001 and $250,000 of shares in Exxon.

Trump entered the war with between $3.2 million and $12.5 million invested in Exxon, according to his financial disclosures. By market close on Aug. 31, the rise in Exxon's share price had added an estimated $176,000 to $690,000 to that initial stake, before accounting for later trades, based on a CNBC analysis of Trump's holdings and share prices.

"Everything that has happened with oil has been directly tied to the largest oil supply disruption in history from the war," saidPavel Molchanov, a senior investment strategist who covers the energy sector at Raymond James & Associates. "Oil is a global commodity, so no one is immune from price increases."

Three weeks after the March 2 purchases, on March 23, Trumppostponed threatened strikeson Iranian energy infrastructure before the market opened, citing "very good and productive conversations."

Brent crudeplunged nearly11%on the prospect of de-escalation. That day, Trump's accounts reported 16 oil and gas stock buys and no sales, worth a combined approximately $163,000 to $570,000, including shares of Exxon, Chevron and Phillips 66.

"Trump's work to get a ceasefire directly played into investment decisions his accounts were pursuing and benefiting for the president," Greytak told CNBC.

The timing of sales is equally striking, watchdogs say.

On April 7, a Trump investment account reported selling between $500,001 and $1 million in Exxon shares. A little more than two and a half hours after the market closed, Trump announced atwo-week ceasefirewith Iran.

Exxon opened more than6% lowerthe next morning. If the shares sold had been held since before the war, CNBC estimates that, in addition to averting the next day's loss, they had gained roughly $35,000 to $70,000 since Feb. 27. The disclosures do not identify the purchase dates for the shares that were sold, so the estimate does not represent the transaction's actual profit.

In all, Trump's accounts reported at least 23 sales involving the nine companies through June 29, the latest transaction date disclosed. If those shares had been held since before the war, CNBC estimates they would have been worth $36,000 to $95,000 more when sold than on Feb. 27 — a fraction of the larger paper gains Trump continued to hold.

"The optics of avoiding thousands in losses right before a market-moving announcement are impossible to defend," Sherman told CNBC. "The selling is just the tip of the iceberg."

Democratic staff on the congressional Joint Economic Committee estimated in anAugust reportthat Trump's broader oil and gas portfolio had increased in value by as much as $15.5 million this year.

"Donald Trump held millions in oil and gas company stocks at the end of 2025. Today, those stocks are worth as much as $15.5 million more," Sen.Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass.,wrote on Xfollowing the report. "What happened? He started a war with Iran this year — and sent oil and gas stocks soaring."

Trump's energy holdings are part of broader financial interests related to the Middle East, including tens of millions of dollars in income from a boomingforeign real-estate licensing business.

Several congressional Democrats have raised the prospect ofinvestigating Trump'sstock trading and his family's business ventures if they win control of either chamber of Congress in November's midterm election.

On Aug. 27, Rep.Jamie Raskin, D-Md., opened an investigation into1789 Capital, whereDonald Trump Jr.is a partner,alleging the firm benefited from Trumpadministration contracts, funding and regulatory actions. Trump Jr.told The Guardianthe allegations were "unsubstantiated talking points."

The war's disruptions have delivered a windfall for oil companies while driving up costs for consumers.

The nine energy companies in Trump's portfolio reported a combined $47.6 billion in second-quarter profit, triple the $15.9 billion they earned a year earlier, according to a CNBC analysis of company filings.

ExxonandChevron, Trump's two largest energy holdings, reported a combined $26.6 billion in profit, up from $9.6 billion a year earlier as higher oil prices and refining margins lifted earnings. Marathon, Phillips 66 andValero, three refiners in his portfolio, collectively reported another $12.7 billion in combined second-quarter profit.

The forces driving those profits — and raising costs for consumers — could persist. On Exxon's July 31earnings call, CEO Darren Woods said refining capacity relative to demand was the tightest he had seen outside the pandemic. "These high margins lead to high product prices," he said.

Phillips 66 CEOMark Lashierstruck a similar note Aug. 5 in his company's earnings call,sayingrefining conditions would remain strong "even if peace broke out tomorrow."

That could prove politically toxic in the midterm election, based on polling.

Affordabilityissues such as gas prices are dominating the midterm campaign: 48% of Americans rank the cost of living as their top voting issue, while 70% disapprove of Trump's handling of it, according to an early AugustReuters/Ipsos pollof 4,505 general population adults aged 18 or older, with a margin of error of plus or minus 1.5 percentage points.

title: 谷歌将在“欧洲的德克萨斯”投资创纪录的 150 亿美元人工智能基础设施
content:
谷歌周三表示，将在芬兰的人工智能基础设施上投资至少 130 亿欧元（151 亿美元），这是这家科技巨头在欧洲最大的单笔投资。

在人工智能热潮中，芬兰已成为数据中心的关键地点，超大规模企业和开发商都在关注其可用的土地和电力，而欧洲大部分地区的土地和电力都供不应求。

谷歌将在 2028 年之前部署这笔资金，包括数据中心和数据中心。该公司在一份声明中表示，能源项目等其他支持性投资。

该公司补充说，它已与芬兰能源公司 Fortum 签署了一份为期 22 年的延长寿命购电协议 (PPA)，该消息一出，该公司的股价就上涨了 11%。

“Google 很自豪能够通过该公司在欧洲最大的单笔投资加深我们在芬兰的根基，这是建立在对芬兰超过 15 年持续投资的基础上的，”Alphabet 和 Alphabet 的总裁兼首席投资官露丝·波拉特 (Ruth Porat) 说道。 Google 在一份声明中表示。

“这项投资突显了 Google 致力于以负责任的方式发展我们的业务，将我们的技术基础设施的扩展与新能源容量、电网增强和能源可承受性计划相结合。”

近几个月来，芬兰宣布了几个潜在容量达数百兆瓦的数据中心项目。

Pure DC 在 7 月份表示，将投资 15 亿欧元（17.4 亿美元）在芬兰建造一个 110 兆瓦的园区，并有可能扩大到 550 兆瓦以上。 Arcem 计划建设一个容量高达 500 兆瓦的站点。今年 3 月，Nebius 公布了在芬兰建设欧洲最大人工智能工厂之一的计划。

“芬兰目前对人工智能基础设施的需求巨大，我在行业活动中听说它被称为‘欧洲的德克萨斯’，”芬兰 Hannes Snellman 律师事务所房地产合伙人 Matti Lajunen 告诉 CNBC。 “我们现在看到的是，每周都会有新参与者询问进入芬兰市场的情况。”

德克萨斯州已成为全球 AI 数据中心的领先地点之一，包括 Meta、Microsoft 和 Anthropic 在内的超大规模企业和 AI 实验室宣布了许多大型项目。谷歌去年 11 月表示，到 2027 年将在德克萨斯州投资 400 亿美元。

谷歌表示，将与 Fortum 一起，在芬兰南部小镇洛维萨 (Loviisa) 基地“努力寻找新的商业模式，以提高潜在新型核反应堆的商业可行性”。

芬兰也是支持社交媒体工作负载的数字基础设施的一个有吸引力的地点，TikTok 计划扩大其在该国的数据中心容量。

“价值数据经济的作用远远超出了直接投资的范围，还促进了创新、研究和开发。”芬兰总理佩特里·奥尔波 (Petteri Orpo) 说道。 “加深我们与 Google 的合作将为双方带来持久的利益。”

content: 图片来源，盖蒂图片社作者：Emer Moreau，商业记者和凯蒂·奥斯汀，交通通讯员发布2026 年 9 月 9 日，英国夏令时 09:50 更新于 11 分钟前 根据最新数据，尽管试图减少延误，但学员司机在预订实际考试之前平均需要等待 20 周。驾驶员和车辆标准局 (DVSA) 8 月份的数据仅比 2026 年 8 月的数据略有改善。 7 月为 20.2 周。预约和参加考试之间的平均等待时间保持在 11.1 周不变。DVSA 最初的目标是到去年年底将平均等待时间减少到 7 周。交通部长海蒂·亚历山大 (Heidi Alexander) 将这一目标推迟到 2026 年夏季，但随后承认这也是不可能的。DVSA 今年早些时候对其实际驾驶考试预订系统进行了多项更改。现在只有学员自己可以预订驾驶考试，从而阻止教练或第三方使用学习者的详细信息进行预订。还有一个地理限制，这意味着学习者只能在其三个当地考试中心预订考试，而不能在该国另一端的考试中心预订考试，如果DVSA 周三表示，截至 2026 年 8 月的 12 个月内进行了超过 213 万次实际驾驶考试，这是有记录以来 12 个月的最高数字。DVSA 首席执行官贝弗利·沃明顿 (Beverley Warmington) 表示：“还有更多工作要做，直到每个学习者都能获得公平的考试为止，我们不会停止。”当他们需要时，但今天的数据表明我们的计划正在发挥作用。“相关主题英国驾驶执照更多关于这个故事如何改变学习司机的驾驶考试预订发布6月9日发布驾驶测试等待时间目标要到明年秋季才能实现发布17月”

title: 随着贸易战升级，美国宣布对大量加拿大商品实施进口禁令
content:
白宫表示，由于与渥太华的外交和贸易关系继续恶化，将从本月晚些时候开始禁止进口加拿大摩托车和一系列其他产品。

美国唐纳德·特朗普总统周一晚间发布了一系列行政命令，宣布禁止加拿大乳清产品和糖蜜、无酒精啤酒以及一系列酒精饮料，包括麦芽啤酒、葡萄酒、苹果酒、威士忌、伏特加和其他烈酒。更大容量的摩托车和轻便摩托车也将被禁止。

进口限制将于2026年9月29日生效，很大程度上取代50%的关税。

美国还宣布将从9月15日起修改和延长对加拿大其他产品的关税，包括增加全地形车和兽皮，取消岩盐和兽皮。水泥。

美国贸易代表杰米森·格里尔 (Jamieson Greer) 表示，这些举措是“加拿大继续对美国关键出口产品实行歧视性待遇的自然结果。”

同日宣布，加拿大对价值 276 亿加元的美国进口产品征收关税，针对钢铁、乳制品、农业设备、纸浆和纸张、电子产品等 700 多种商品。

渥太华此前表示，这些关税是“一元对一元”的回应。贸易谈判在 8 月 21 日最后期限前惨然破裂后，美国于 8 月对本国商品征收 50% 的关税。

双方继续互相指责对方未能达成协议，并指责对方采取不公平做法伤害本国工人。

特朗普指责加拿大通过汽车、酒精和乳制品行业的政策损害美国出口，这凸显了美国的做法。商品贸易逆差，并威胁从 2027 年 1 月 1 日起对汽车、卡车和汽车零部件征收 50% 的关税。

加拿大总理马克·卡尼 (Mark Carney) 在 8 月的一次讲话中表示，“商品贸易逆差之所以小幅存在，只是因为美国从我们这里购买了如此多的能源”，并指出加拿大是美国汽车和钢铁的最大消费国。

他还表示，美国“要求美国” ”在贸易谈判中“采取了太多措施”，即使经济受到打击并减少消费者的选择，也需要采取报复措施来保护加拿大工人和公司。

现有关税仅适用于两国之间 7155 亿美元货物贸易中相对较小的一部分，但经济学家警告称，中小型企业将立即受到打击，并且进一步升级将给经济增长带来风险。

“边境两侧的公司将需要等待礼德史密斯律师事务所国际贸易和国家安全小组助理 Justin Angotti 表示：“为了看看这些关税是否有效，会颁布更多措施，或者每个国家都决定降级。与此同时，这些企业将面临关税、合规和不确定性相关的成本。”

据彭博社周二报道，随着与华盛顿的关系恶化，渥太华正在考虑与欧盟建立更密切的贸易和安全关系。

啤酒和啤酒随着美国和加拿大关系恶化，烈酒销售已成为政治热点。

加拿大多个省份的商店已将美国酒类下架，公众运动呼吁抵制，萨斯喀彻温省省长斯科特·莫 (Scott Moe) 于 8 月宣布对美国进口产品征收 50% 的关税。

莫伊的团队本周向 CNBC 表示，酒类税是一项“对等措施”，旨在支持当地企业并鼓励在公平和平衡的贸易解决方案方面取得进展。

美国根据美国蒸馏酒理事会的数据，从 2025 年 3 月报复性禁令开始到 2025 年 12 月，对加拿大的烈酒出口同比下降了 70% 以上。

该行业协会主席兼首席执行官克里斯·斯旺格 (Chris Swonger) 表示，美国酿酒商“首当其冲地承受了这场贸易争端。”

“我们感谢特朗普总统认识到这些销售禁令的重大危害。斯旺格说：“这已经引起了美国酿酒商的关注，并敦促两国领导人通过谈判达成解决方案，使美国烈酒重新回到加拿大各地的零售货架上，并使烈酒行业恢复到永久的零对零关税框架。”

—CNBC 的布兰登·戈麦斯 (Brandon Gomez) 对本文做出了贡献。

title: 克里姆林宫称，特朗普告诉普京，随着乌克兰战争迅速结束，美俄关系可以“全面恢复”
content:
美国据克里姆林宫宣读的两国领导人通话内容，唐纳德·特朗普总统告诉俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京，迅速解决乌克兰战争可能为两国全面恢复贸易和经济关系铺平道路。

据称，特朗普和普京就美国特使史蒂夫·威特科夫和贾里德·库什纳最近访问莫斯科和基辅的结果交换了意见，美国特使史蒂夫·威特科夫和贾里德·库什纳寻求重振陷入僵局的外交关系。会谈以结束冲突。

在周末美国和平谈判代表访问短暂暂停后，俄罗斯恢复了对乌克兰主要城市的空袭。乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基周三表示，国际社会对最近的致命袭击“反应太少”。

克里姆林宫助手尤里·乌沙科夫表示，据俄罗斯塔斯社报道，特朗普和普京周二进行了整整一个小时的交谈，称这次谈话“具有建设性且非常坦诚”。

特朗普明确表示，他希望乌克兰战争早日爆发。乌沙科夫表示，“尽快”结束，并补充说普京向特朗普就俄罗斯所谓的特种军事行动进行了“客观、彻底”的分析。

特朗普表示，迅速结束俄罗斯对乌克兰的全面入侵“将立即为美俄关系全面恢复开辟令人印象深刻且影响深远的前景”。

普京还分享了他对美国方面可以采取哪些行动来迅速提供帮助的看法。乌沙科夫补充说，结束在乌克兰的军事行动，并驳斥了有关俄罗斯对欧洲国家构成威胁的猜测。

周三上午，当 CNBC 联系到白宫发言人时，并未立即发表评论。

根据塔斯社的计算，这次通话是普京今年与特朗普的第五次通话，也是自美国总统 2025 年初上任以来两国领导人的第 15 次通话。

乌克兰泽连斯基多次对即将到来的冬季发出警报，呼吁盟国提供进一步支持，提供急需的拦截导弹。

由于基辅面临防空设备短缺的问题，俄罗斯军队加大了对乌克兰城市的导弹袭击次数。

乌克兰则对俄罗斯炼油厂和物流中心进行远程无人机袭击，寻求提高莫斯科的战争成本和试验成本。普京在经历了四年半的冲突后的决心。

title: 人类研究人员表示，在同事辞职后，人工智能有超过 10% 的机会“杀死所有人类”
content:
周二，一位 Anthropic 安全研究人员表示，人工智能有超过 10% 的可能性“杀死所有人类”。几小时后，另一名员工表示，他因担心人工智能实验室“拿我们的生命做赌注”而辞职。

这些评论凸显了人工智能开发核心人士日益担心的问题，即尽管 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 继续筹集大量资金，但人工智能可能会失控并对人类构成威胁。并朝着预期的公开上市迈进。

Anthropic 研究员雅各布·考克森 (Jacob Coxon) 周二表示，他从公司辞职。 Coxon 表示，Anthropic 和 OpenAI 都没有采取负责任的行动。

Coxon 在 onX 的一篇帖子中表示：“他们正在直接竞速自我改进的超级智能，并拿我们的生命进行赌博。”

自我改进是指人工智能系统可以在没有太多人类干预的情况下自我改进。通常所说的递归自我完善目前还不可能实现，但人工智能实验室正在朝着这个目标努力。

“不要低估这项技术的力量。这些很快就会成为超人系统，可以破解任何东西，在一夜之间彻底改变任何领域，并获得真正的力量和资源。我们都见证了这些领域的进展，而且进展并没有放缓，”考克森说。

他补充说，“构建人工智能的人们真诚地相信， ”

这一评论引起了 Anthropic 的对齐科学主管 Evan Hubinger 的回应，他说 Coxon 的说法不仅是“正确的”，而且 Anthropic 没有针对这种情况的计划。

“Jacob 在这里是正确的——我们确实真诚地相信人工智能可以杀死所有人类！我个人认为在未来十年内它会超过 10%，我相信 Anthropic 正在尝试它。最好的，但我们还没有解决超级智能对齐问题的计划，也没有明确的进展。”Hubinger 在 onX 上说道。

当 CNBC 联系到 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 时，我们没有立即发表评论。

6 月份，Anthropic 指出“完全递归的自我改进也可能会增加人类失去对人工智能系统控制的风险。”

“如果系统能够完全构建Anthropic 在一篇博客文章中表示：“他们自己的继任者，我们保护他们、监控他们和塑造他们行为的方式都变得更加重要。”

对人工智能失控的担忧并不新鲜。特斯拉和 SpaceX 首席执行官埃隆·马斯克在过去几年中警告称，人工智能可能对人类构成威胁。主要研究人员和学者也对公司失去对人工智能系统的控制敲响了警钟。

在 OpenAI 模型于 7 月份失控并破坏了开源开发者的主要平台 Hugging Face 后，这些担忧有所加剧。

Coxon 引用 Hugging Face 事件作为“警告镜头”的一个例子，该事件使美国实验室之间的协议更加可行，使他对协调的潜力更加乐观。但 Coxon 警告称，全球人工智能竞赛将不可避免。

“我不认为我们正在阻止全球人工智能竞赛，这可能需要采取代价高昂的行动，例如暂时禁止改进模型能力，”Coxon 说。

title: OpenAI 声称在 88 小时内解决了 90 年前的纳维-斯托克斯数学难题
content:
OpenAI 表示，它使用 10,000 个代理和新的人工智能模型，在 88 小时内解决了 90 年之久的纳维-斯托克斯数学问题。

在周二发布的一份新闻稿中，ChatGPT AI 聊天机器人背后的公司 OpenAI 表示，它正在“共享该问题的解决方案”，该解决方案与流体如何移动有关。

它表示，它使用了一个“协调系统”代理”由其内部人工智能模型提供支持。

“代理可以使用各种工具，例如从互联网缓存版本中读取数据的能力以及运行代码的能力。代理被细分为能够在组内进行通信的组。”OpenAI 表示。 “各个小组的规模各不相同，产生纳维-斯托克斯决议的小组涉及大约 10,000 个并发代理。”

“这些代理于 9 月 5 日星期六，即第一批代理启动后大约 88 小时得出了他们的决议，”该公司补充道。

纳维-斯托克斯是七个千年奖问题之一，被认为是本研究开始时最困难的数学问题之一。创立该奖项的马萨诸塞州剑桥克莱数学研究所尚未对 OpenAI 提出的解决方案发表评论。

然而，OpenAI 的工作引起了纽约大学数学教授特里斯坦·巴克马斯特 (Tristan Buckmaster) 的质疑。

巴克马斯特在其网站上的一份声明中解释说，他一直在与在 OpenAI 竞争对手 Anthropic 工作的数学家同事 Levent Alpöge 合作，

他说 Alpöge 收到“提示”，称两人的进展信息已传递给 OpenAI。他表示，这家科技巨头的解决方案路线与他们自己的工作类似，“这不是通过给模型提供问题陈述而在几天内达到的方向。”

Buckmaster 还提出了 OpenAI 模型是否接受过 OpenAI Codex 中的训练或访问其会话的疑问。他说数学家们在他们的工作中使用了几种大型语言模型。

巴克马斯特补充道：“我想澄清一下我没有声明的内容。我还没有看到 OpenAI 的证明。我不知道他们的模型做了什么，也不知道如何使用。我不知道我们的数据是否被使用。”

在声明中，OpenAI 表示，在“听到该公司补充道，“在他们公开发布之前，我们（研究人员和代理人）没有通过任何方式看到他们的任何工作，特别是，没有为了解决这个问题而访问任何特定的用户数据，尽管可能性不大，但我们不能排除从他们使用我们产品中获得的去识别数据有助于改进我们的模型”。

克莱数学研究所成立。 2000 年设立了问题奖，为每个问题的解决设立 100 万美元的奖金。

“该奖项的设立是为了提高公众的意识，即数学领域的前沿仍然是开放的，并且存在大量未解决的重要问题；强调努力解决最深刻、最困难问题的重要性；并表彰具有历史意义的数学成就，”该研究所在其声明中表示。网站。

其他问题包括与椭圆曲线相关的伯奇和斯温纳顿-戴尔猜想，以及与素数相关的黎曼猜想。

title: 美伊针锋相对引发石油供应担忧布伦特原油徘徊在100美元附近
content:
油价周三上涨，国际基准布伦特原油期货短暂突破 100 美元关口，因美国和伊朗之间的紧张局势升级加剧了人们对中东能源供应进一步中断的担忧。

布伦特原油期货最后交易价格约为每桶 99.93 美元，此前于美国东部时间凌晨 3:20 左右上涨至每桶 100.01 美元。该合约上次上涨至 100 美元以上是在 7 月份。

美国11 月交割的基准西德克萨斯中质原油期货价格上涨 1.7%，至每桶 94.58 美元。

美国军方周二摧毁了五艘伊朗原油油轮，以报复一艘美国军舰遭到袭击的企图。 美国中央司令部在声明中表示，美国军舰成功躲避了伊朗的袭击，没有美国人员受伤。

高盛全球大宗商品研究联席主管达安·斯特鲁文 (Daan Struyven) 表示，美伊冲突升级现已进入第七个月，随着对航运的攻击加剧，油价飙升至每桶 120 美元以上的风险。

“这绝对是当被问及油价能否达到每桶 120 美元时，斯特鲁文告诉 CNBC 的“Squawk Box Asia”节目，这似乎是合理的。高盛的基本预测仍然是，随着生产商适应中断，包括通过替代运输路线和最终增加管道容量，波斯湾出口将逐步恢复。

但他表示，最近的升级增加了未来几个月出口未能恢复的更乐观情景的可能性。

“过去几天的事态发展确实表明，另一种价格上行情景是，未来几个月出口实际上停滞不前，布伦特原油价格超过120 美元是这种情况的可能性肯定会上升，因为我们看到航运袭击的加剧和扩大。”Struyven 说。

美国与伊朗的军事行动已经暂停了大约一个月，华盛顿转向对德黑兰施加经济压力，直到上个月月底才恢复袭击。

title: 如果我的航班取消或延误，我有什么权利？
content: Image source,AFP via Getty ImagesPublished31 May 2022Updated 1 hour agoThousands of air passengers have seen their travel plans disrupted after an air traffic control problemgrounded nearly 2,000 flights across the UK.When a flight is cancelled or delayed, passengers affected have various rights â such as a refund or be put on another flight. However, these can vary depending on which carrier you are flying with and from where.Only when an airline is at fault - not issues such as air traffic control problems - is extra compensation payable. Here's what it means for you.What do airlines have to offer passengers?When flights are delayed or cancelled, UK and EU airlines, and other carriers when you are departing a UK or EU airport, have a duty to look after you.The reason for the delay or cancellation does not matter. So anyone affected by the air transport delays will be eligible.That includes providing meals and accommodation, if necessary, and getting you to your destination. The airline should organise putting you on an alternative flight, at no extra cost.Additional losses, such as unused accommodation, might require a claim to a credit card provider, if that was the payment option used.After that, a claim may need to go to your travel insurance provider. But there is no standard definition of what is covered.It may require a close look at the details of the policy to see what is covered, and in which circumstances.Passengers are also being urged to heedtravel advice from the UK government,external, as this can also affect travel insurance rights.If my flight is cancelled, can I get a refund or another flight?If your flight is covered by UK law, your airline must let you choose between either getting a refund or being booked on to an alternative flight.That's regardless of how far in advance the cancellation was made.You can get your money back for any part of the ticket you have not used.So, if you booked a return flight and the outbound leg is cancelled, you can get the full cost of the return ticket refunded.If you still want to travel, your airline must find you an alternative flight.If another airline is flying to your destination significantly sooner, or there are other suitable modes of transport, then you have a right to be booked on to that alternative transport instead.If your flight was coming into the UK on a non-UK or EU airline, then you should check the terms and conditions of your booking.How do I renew my UK passport and what is the 10-year rule?,externalThree things you can do to stop EU border checks at the airport costing youWill the airline pay for food and accommodation?If you are stuck abroad or at the airport because of a flight cancellation, airlines covered by UK legislation must also provide you with other assistance.This includes:a reasonable amount of food and drink (often in the form of vouchers)a way for you to communicate (often by refunding the cost of calls)free accommodation, if you have to stay overnight to fly the next daytransport to and from the accommodationIf your airline is unable to arrange assistance, you have the right to organise this yourself and claim back the cost later.The Civil Aviation Authority advises people to keep receipts and not spend more than necessary.Civil Aviation Authority: Delays and cancellations,externalYou are entitled to the same assistance as for a cancellation if your flight is delayed by more than two hours for a short-haul flight, three hours for a medium-haul, or four hours for a long-haul.If you are delayed by more than five hours and no longer want to travel, you can get a full refund.What are my rights if I have booked a package holiday?If you booked a package holiday with a company that is an ABTA member and your flight is cancelled, you are entitled to a suitable alternative flight or a full refund.ABTA: What are your rights?,externalCan I claim extra compensation for disruption?Disruption caused by things like air traffic control issues â but also bad weather, strikes by airport staff, or conflict, or other "extraordinary circumstances" â does not entitle you to extra compensation.However, in other circumstances, when it is considered to be the airline's fault,you have a number of rights under UK law,external.These apply as long as you are flying from a UK airport on any airline, arriving at a UK airport on an EU or UK airline, or arriving at an airport in the EU on a UK airline.What you are entitled to depends on what caused the cancellation and how much notice you are given.If your flight is cancelled with less than two weeks' notice, you may be able to claim compensation based on the timings of the alternative flight you are offered.The amount you are entitled to also depends on how far you were travelling:for flightsunder 1,500km, such as Glasgow to Amsterdam, you can claim up to Â£220 per personfor flights of1,500km to 3,500km, such as East Midlands to Marrakesh, you can claimup to Â£350 per personfor flights over3,500km, such as London to New York, you can claimup to Â£520 per personWhat if flight delays mean I am late for work?Airlines will not refund you for loss of earnings. Travel insurance policies will not usually cover loss of earnings either.If you think you're going to be late back at work because of flight delays, you have a responsibility to let your employer know, legal experts say.You should agree with your employer how to deal with the absence â for example, by using annual leave or taking unpaid leave.Employers have no legal obligation to pay employees who are absent in this situation, experts say, unless it is stated in their contract.Get in touchHave your travel plans been disrupted? title: 日本航运巨头董事长表示，日元波动可能导致全球市场“混乱”
content:
一位航运高管表示，虽然日元疲软有利于在其他地方开展业务的日本公司，但日元的大幅波动可能会成为一个问题。

董事长桥本武 (Takeshi Hashimoto) 表示，商船三井的收入主要以美元计价，因此该公司受益于日元贬值。 Mitsui OSK 是全球最大的油轮所有者和运营商，也是最大的航运公司之一。

他在接受 CNBC 的 Lisa Kim 采访时表示，“我们担心（日元疲软）会在金融市场造成混乱的局面。”

桥本告诉 CNBC，他希望看到的是一个稳定的货币市场，并补充说，日元兑美元汇率在 150-155 之间的区间将是“舒适的”。日元最近交投于 153 附近。

近几个月来，日本货币大幅波动，在 2026 年触及数十年来的低点，之后东京的多次干预（华盛顿的联合干预）使日元在一段时间内走强。

当被问及对霍尔木兹海峡的前景时，桥本表示，他对日本航运业的快速复苏感到悲观。

“目前，我们几乎不可能恢复海峡的正常服务。”分析公司 Kpler 周一发布的数据显示，过去 10 天平均每天有 10 艘商船通过霍尔木兹海峡，这是自 5 月份以来的最低数量。

他希望伊朗与阿曼等波斯湾国家之间的谈判能够出现“相当好的局面”。卡塔尔，但也表示这“需要一些时间”。

title: 新加坡男子在美国承认大规模加密货币盗窃罪
content: 图片来源，布劳沃德县治安官办公室 图片说明，22 岁的马龙·林 (Malone Lam) 被指控组织一群朋友窃取加密货币 由商业记者彼得·霍斯金斯 (Peter Hoskins) 和凯莉·吴 (Kelly Ng) 报道，来自新加坡的报道 2026 年 9 月 9 日，英国夏令时间 04:40 更新于 3 小时前 一名新加坡男子周二在美国认罪，罪名是组织敲诈勒索共谋指控这是有史以来最大的加密货币盗窃案之一。马龙·林 (Malone Lam) 承认与朋友联手窃取了 2.45 亿美元（1.81 亿英镑）的比特币，并对所得收益进行洗钱。据美国司法部 (DOJ) 称，这名 22 岁的男子和他的同伙利用这些钱每晚在夜总会消费高达 50 万美元。它还说，他们购买了一批异国情调的汽车，价值从 10 万美元到 380 万美元不等。林面临最高 20 年监禁。美国地区法官科琳·科拉尔-科泰利没有立即为他安排量刑听证会。美国检察官珍妮·皮罗表示，“如果你建立了一个网络犯罪帝国，我们会找到你，瓦解你的业务，并追究你的责任。”她补充道，“这名被告领导一个国际网络，通过欺骗手段掠夺受害者，侵犯他们的隐私，窃取了数亿美元的加密货币。”图片来源，美国司法部图片说明，在美国发布的图片中当局称，2024 年 9 月，林郑月娥被发现持有大量现金在迈阿密一家夜总会参加派对。林郑月娥告诉美国调查人员，他 14 岁时就从新加坡的中学辍学。他于 2023 年 10 月前往美国，并在次年 1 月签证到期后留在美国。根据法庭文件，该阴谋不晚于 2023 年 10 月开始，至少持续到 2025 年 5 月。来自加利福尼亚州、康涅狄格州、纽约州、佛罗里达州和美国境外的同谋者通过在线游戏平台会面。司法部表示，林姆（又名安妮·海瑟薇、$$$ 和 King Greavy）是该犯罪集团的头目，他确定了受害者并协调了不同同谋者的角色。他们诱骗人们泄露机密信息，并偶尔进行入室盗窃，以获取详细信息，从而使他们能够盗取受害者的加密货币钱包。据司法部称，被盗的加密货币还被用来购买价值数万美元的 Hermes Birkin 手袋，这些手袋被扔到夜总会派对的人群中。司法部表示，这些收益用于购买的其他物品包括价值高达 50 万美元的高端手表、价值数万美元的豪华服装、洛杉矶、汉普顿和迈阿密的出租房屋、旅行用的私人飞机租赁以及私人保安团队图片来源，美国司法部 图片说明，美国当局还公布了这张林郑月娥集团使用的超级跑车图片 图片来源，美国司法部 图片说明，美国当局从林郑月娥位于迈阿密的出租屋中查获了多双名牌鞋 佛罗里达地方法院早些时候审理称，林郑月娥因其浮夸的生活方式而在洛杉矶和迈阿密夜店场景中“臭名昭著”，而他的加密货币横财也引起了人们的关注。 2024 年 9 月，美国地方法官艾丽西亚·瓦莱 (Alicia Valle) 首次出庭时表示，“当我听取证据时，我只能想到费里斯·布勒 (Ferris Bueller) 变坏了。”她指的是 1986 年的电影，讲述的是一个男孩假装生病逃学并在芝加哥周围进行疯狂冒险的故事。“（他）花掉了这笔钱，去洛杉矶的夜总会，购买了 30 多辆高端豪华汽车。我的意思是，法官表示，在他获得超过 2.3 亿美元之后，发生了令人难以置信的巨额支出和疯狂行为。今年 4 月，林郑月娥的同谋之一埃文·坦格曼 (Evan Tangeman) 因洗钱计划收益被判处 70 个月监禁。司法部表示，在林郑月娥被捕后，坦格曼还试图销毁证据，法院将其视为“他有罪意识”。商业加密货币比特币犯罪新加坡

title: 美国对加拿大酒类和其他商品实施进口禁令
content: 图片来源，Getty Images发布2026年9月9日，英国夏令时00:42更新20分钟前随着加拿大对美国商品征收报复性关税生效，美国将禁止进口加拿大产品，包括酒类、乳制品和机动车辆。美国总统唐纳德·特朗普在周二的一系列行政命令中写道，“加拿大事实上歧视美国的商业”，并下令实施进口禁令，该禁令将于29日开始实施9月。周二早些时候，加拿大总理马克·卡尼在视频讲话中表示，加拿大摆脱美国作为其最大贸易伙伴的地位“将付出代价”。美国和加拿大官员均表示愿意达成协议，但自8月底谈判破裂以来，尚未安排新的谈判。上个月，在几轮谈判破裂后，白宫对约200亿美元（148亿英镑）的加拿大商品征收50%的关税。作为回应，对钢铁、服装和家具等美国商品征收报复性关税。反关税于周二午夜后生效。美国和加拿大之间的紧张局势也超出了关税范围。今年8月，特朗普下令将安大略湖更名为美洲湖，引起加拿大人和部分美国人的轩然大波。这一突发新闻报道正在更新，更多细节将很快公布。请刷新页面以获取完整版本。您可以通过 BBC 新闻应用程序在智能手机或平板电脑上接收突发新闻。您还可以关注@BBCBreaking on X,external获取最新快讯。相关话题加拿大美国贸易贸易战

title: 晋升是否应该取决于员工如何使用人工智能？
content: Image source,Duncan TrevithickImage caption,Duncan Trevithick's firm has a bonus scheme based on the use of AIByMaryLou CostaTechnology reporterPublished1 hour agoIt's in Duncan Trevithick's interest to be good at using AI at work - if he can use it to get more tasks done, faster, he'll qualify for a bonus at the end of the year.On the surface, it's a great incentive. But he's questioning what's really in it for him."The uncomfortable interpretation is that employees are being assessed on how effectively they can participate in their own redundancy," says Spain-based Trevithick, 34, who works in marketing for an AI training data company.But if he uses AI to take care of two days worth of work each week, he says the financial rewards don't add up."I do not receive two days off or a 40% pay rise. The higher output simply becomes the new baseline. In the short term, that may help me get promoted. In the longer term, I have helped prove how much of my job no longer requires me," he says."I'm just trying to view myself as a manager, and I'm managing some people, and I'm also managing AI agents, or AI loops, or whatever you want to call it."Image source,Los Angeles Times via Getty ImagesImage caption,Coinbase chief executive Brian Armstrong fired staff for not completing AI trainingUsing employees' AI abilities as a measure of whether they should get a bonus, promoted - or even sacked - is fast becoming more common.Accenture CEO Julie Sweet told the Rapid Response podcast in March: "Today, AI at Accenture is how we do work. So if you want to get promoted, you've got to do the things that we do in order to operate at Accenture."And big names like Disney, Meta, JP Morgan and KPMG have introduced "AI leaderboards" to track and rank employees' usage of the array of LLMs and platforms at their disposal,according to media reports,external. Crypto trading platform Coinbase has already fired engineers who didn't complete AI training,as requested by the chief executive, Brian Armstrong,external.It demonstrates how eager business leaders are to see a return from their AI investments, especially when 94% of companies have yet to see significant value from AI,according to a report,externalby consultants McKinsey.Employees feel they have to get on board, thanks to the current state of the jobs market - in the UK, vacancieshave hit a five-year low.Meanwhile, 75% of the 1,881 UK jobseekers polled in July by recruiter Gi Group say they would not be put off applying to an organisation that had introduced AI proficiency into individual performance reviews. Around 22% said it would be off-putting."It's like being in the sea and you see a giant wave coming. You can get out a surfboard and try and ride it as long as possible, or you can just let it take you under. But you can't stop the wave," says Trevithick.But what's going on at the large consultancy Pamela (her name has been changed to protect her identity) works for isn't sitting right with her.She's a US-based senior executive who has observed that, while there isn't a formal mandate for employees to use AI, it's obviously determining who is rewarded, and who is left behind."The ground is shifting under us. You've got to demonstrate [AI] fluency and fluidity as one of your key achievements. It's kind of quiet where nobody's saying, 'learn AI or else'. But let me tell you, in performance reviews, they reward who uses it well," says Pamela.That shift, she adds, means that AI capabilities are now counting for more than actual experience, which is creating a "two tier workforce"."You've got the same job title, same tenure, but different value based on whether someone treats AI as a threat or a tool - that gap widens really quickly once leadership notices it," says Pamela."AI fluency beats credentials every day. Somebody that has 15, 20 years of experience and no AI fluency will be passed over for those that have, say, three years, but are fast with the tools."She adds: "If you're not visibly using AI, you see slower promotion timelines. It's harder to be seen, and it's harder to fight being on that shortlist."Image source,WeightmansImage caption,The use of AI raises questions of fairness says Tina ChanderBut is it legal for companies to shift the goal posts like this?Legally, bosses are in the clear, confirms Tina Chander, partner and employment lawyer at Weightmans. But she says it does open up questions about pay and fairness."The question then becomes whether the employer increases expectations on the basis that the employee can now produce more work. Is that fair?" questions Chander."And if an employee is effectively doing more because AI has made them more efficient, should they be rewarded differently? Or are they effectively making themselves redundant, thus acting as a disincentive to be productive?"Chander advises businesses to have clear policies, training and boundaries in place, otherwise they risk employees opening up disputes about fairness, performance expectations and job security.Indeed, from January 2027, UK employees will have six months to submit unfair dismissal claims compared with the current three months, and will be able to do soafter just six months service, rather than the current two years.Yet HR consultant Tina Rahman says employers aren't currently being transparent enough in telling employees why they want AI to be part of people's jobs, and what the end purpose of that is - which she agrees is to save costs and time, but also to cut down on outsourcing."Because they misunderstand it, this is not being reflected to employees," says Rahman, who runs a London-based consultancy, HR Habitat.Image source,Tina RahmanImage caption,Employers need to be transparent about AI expectations says Tina RahmanA lack of clarity around AI usage is certainly causing discontent at Pamela's company."Leadership is being inconsistent and vague on purpose. Firms want productivity gains without owning the disruption narrative," she says."If something goes wrong, they're going to say, 'I didn't tell you to do that. Where'd you get that from?' Then if you did something with AI, and it works, great."Mandating AI use at work can become purely performative, rather than having any real positive impact, warns Kamila Miller, applied AI researcher and lecturer at Henley Business School."Make AI usage a KPI [key performance indicator], and people will log their interactions to hit the metric, route work through a chatbot that did not need it, and generate AI-flavoured outputs that look productive on a dashboard. You will measure adoption. You will not measure judgement, learning, or better decisions," states Miller, who is based in Reading."You have not made people more skilled - you have made them more obedient."Some firms have acknowledged those arguments.In April, Luis von Ahn, the CEO of Duolingo,told the podcast Silicon Valley Girl,externalthat his language learning firm is no longer using AI use as part of performance reviews."We found that people... were asking: 'Do you want us to use AI for AI's sake?'"In the end we backtracked and we said: 'Look, the most important thing for your performance is that you are doing, whatever your job is, as well as possible. A lot of times AI can help you with that. But if it can't, I'm not going to force you to do that.'"Meanwhile, in May,the Financial Times reported,externalthat Amazon had shut down an internal leaderboard which tracked employee's use of AI. The report said employees had been attempting to climb the rankings by setting AI needless tasks.Image source,Kamilla MillerImage caption,Who gets the blame if AI makes a mistake asks Kamilla MillerDespite those high-profile moves, some staff still they need to show AI proficiency - Pamela is one of those.In her mid 50s, she plans to retire within 10 years, and wants to keep her job so she doesn't risk losing any pension and health benefits. She's visibly stepping up how AI is helping her bring in new clients, and making sure she's being credited for it.As for Duncan Trevithick, he's doing his best to future proof himself with a number of side projects."If AI can do a job better than you can, it makes sense for the business to replace you. That's how the capitalist model works. So it's about, how can you move into a position where you own assets where you can leverage AI, and then you benefit," says Trevithick.Related topicsInternational BusinessTechnology of BusinessArtificial intelligenceCareersPayMore on this storyAI is 'not smart' so what's next in artificial intelligence?Published3 JulyIndia wants to join the strawberry superpowersPublished30 JulyIs it time to stop using glue and labels on paper?Published28 July

title: 股指期货在盘中下跌后变化不大；布伦特原油突破每桶 99 美元：实时更新
content:
随着油价继续上涨，股市期货在经历了一天的下跌之后，周二晚间几乎持平。

道琼斯工业平均指数期货下跌 15 点。标准普尔 500 指数期货和纳斯达克 100 指数期货也接近持平线。

在有报道称伊朗对伊朗发动第二轮攻击后，布伦特原油期货在周二的延长交易中跃升至每桶 99 美元以上。本周美国海军舰艇的情况此前未公开。盘后交易中，美国西德克萨斯中质原油价格攀升至每桶 94 美元以上。

盘后原油价格上涨，此前原油盘中上涨，在假期缩短的交易周的第一个交易日给三大主要均线带来下行压力。周一适逢劳动节假期，股市一片漆黑。

道琼斯指数周二下跌 1.2%，创下近三周来最糟糕的一天。标准普尔 500 指数和纳斯达克综合指数分别下跌 0.6% 和 0.3%。

周二，由于油价上涨加剧了人们对通胀的担忧，10 年期美国国债收益率短暂攀升至备受关注的 4.8% 水平之上。 Kestra 投资管理公司投资主管卡拉·墨菲 (Kara Murphy) 在 CNBC 的“收盘钟”节目中表示，收益率走势进一步打压了股市。

这“有点减速”。 “盈利方面的关注点有所减少，因此我认为市场现在已经将注意力转移到了风险方面。”

周三没有重大经济数据发布或企业盈利报告。本周晚些时候，交易员将监测通胀数据，以了解美联储可能如何调整利率的信号。

以下是一些在延长交易中走势的股票：

与道琼斯指数、标准普尔 500 指数和纳斯达克 100 指数相关的期货下午 6 点后不久均接近持平。美国东部时间周二晚上。

title: 高通和康宁宣布交易后，人工智能基础设施股上涨
content:
康宁和高通周二上涨，并带动了许多人工智能相关股票的上涨，因为两项基础设施交易增强了华尔街对数据中心支出将保持强劲的信心。

芯片制造商英特尔和Advanced Micro Devices分别上涨9%和6%，而惠普企业上涨8%，光子公司相干公司上涨7%。

所有这些股票今年，随着人工基础设施建设扩展到英伟达以外的公司，HPE 和 AMD 的价值增加了一倍以上，英特尔几乎增加了两倍。

玻璃制造商康宁公司的光纤技术正在成为人工智能数据中心的关键部分，该公司周二股价上涨 8%，今年的涨幅达到 90%。该公司表示，正在与 Verizon 建立价值数十亿美元的合作伙伴关系，为人工智能连接建造光纤电缆。 -

今年 6 月，康宁与亚马逊达成了一项价值数十亿美元的交易，一个月前英伟达承诺向该公司投资最多 32 亿美元，在北卡罗来纳州和德克萨斯州建造三个新的光纤制造工厂。

与此同时，高通在周二提交的一份文件中表示，它向亚马逊发行了认股权证，允许这家云巨头收购这家芯片制造商价值最多 40 亿美元的股票。这是两家公司建立人工智能基础设施协议的一部分，亚马逊网络服务公司购买了价值高达 600 亿美元的高通服务器芯片和其他技术。

高通首席财务官 Akash Palkhiwala 周二在旧金山举行的高盛 Communacopia + 技术会议上表示，为亚马逊制造芯片的收入将于 12 月季度开始实现，并将成为帮助该公司实现其目标的“核心组成部分”之一。 2029 财年数据中心收入目标为 150 亿美元。

在 6 月份的投资者日，高通表示正在与两家未具名的数据中心公司合作。其中之一是亚马逊。 Palkhiwala 周二表示，该公司“正在与其他数据中心客户进行类似的处理。”

AMD 首席财务官 Jean Hu 也在高盛活动中发表了讲话。她表示，继首席执行官苏姿丰 (Lisa Su) 在 7 月份表示，到 2028 年半导体行业将达到 2 万亿美元之后，到 2030 年，潜在市场总额将达到 3 万亿美元。

人工智能股票的狂热之际，人工智能和数据中心问题的分歧最为严重。根据 2026 年 5 月盖洛普民意调查，71% 的美国人反对在他们的社区建立数据中心。这直接转化为财务风险，Anthropicpoied 在即将发布的 IPO 招股说明书中将针对人工智能和数据中心的负面公众舆论列为风险因素。
