title: 令人窒息的炎热和破损的厕所：TUI River Cruise 乘客讲述他们的假期地狱
content: Image caption,Andy Peach and his wife spent nearly Â£4,000 for their cruise with TUIByKaty Austin,ÂTransport correspondentÂandÂSimon Browning,ÂTransport reporterPublished15 minutes agoDozens of people have accused TUI River Cruises of operating vessels with faulty facilities including persistently broken air conditioning, after they spent thousands of pounds on holidays.Earlier this year passengers on the Skyla, a ship operated by TUI, contacted BBC Your Voice to say they had beenstranded in Budapest during a heatwave with little to no air conditioning.Following that report more people got in touch to say they faced similar problems on both the Skyla and its sister vessel, the Isla. They criticised TUI's customer service and said the refunds offered were inadequate.TUI apologised to customers where trips "fell short of the standards we aim to deliver".A spokesperson for TUI, said: "We understand the disappointment and frustration caused to affected customers."Passengers described stifling conditions as well as problems with plumbing after paying thousands of pounds for European cruises, including on the Danube River.Andy Peach and his wife booked a seven-day trip on the Skyla in June, travelling through Budapest, Vienna and Linz.It turned out to be "the worst TUI holiday we've ever been on", he said.Instead of air conditioning, Peach said there were "big blowers" on board, expelling hot air."One was in the middle of the corridor, blocking the exit," he said. "It didn't seem to cool the place down."Temperatures onboard climbed as the holiday went on leaving him "exhausted", he said. By the end of the week, Peach said the air conditioning in cabins had broken too.On the second-to-last day passengers were transferred to hotels, which Peach said were "really basic".He and his wife had paid nearly Â£4,000 for the holiday but they were offered only Â£300 as a refund and given 72-hours to accept it.He said: "TUI know there's problems on these boats, but continue to sell them to people as a full luxury cruise."Image source,Andy PeachImage caption,Andy Peach said an air conditioning unit blocked a corridor on the SkylaDuring the time Peach was on the Skyla, Joan Craven came across complaints on social media.She was due to take the ship's next sailing from Budapest a few days later and was worried.TUI's customer services assured her by email that the air conditioning on board was working. When she arrived, however, a holiday rep told her it was not. Craven told the BBC she felt misled.Some people had described issues with air conditioning as well as problems with the water supply on the same vessel in May.Meanwhile, complaints about the Isla go back even further.'A tropical house at a zoo'Wendy Charnley and her husband Rob had "pushed the boat out" to celebrate his retirement by booking a cruise on the Isla in April 2025 departing from Amsterdam.It was like "being in a tropical house at a zoo" Charnley said, with no sign of air conditioning."Some areas were really, really hot." she said. "There wasn't really anywhere that you could go that you could cool down."A couple of months later, Kevin Darvill boarded the ship in Frankfurt.He immediately noticed the toilet didn't work in the reception area. Portable fans and air conditioning units were also visible.Darvill said the ship became "really hot" with "no respite"."It was intolerable because there was literally no air circulation," he said. "The worst places were the restaurants."He struggled to sleep. Meanwhile, his shower alternated between freezing cold and "scalding hot".Image source,AlamyImage caption,Passengers said there were problems on the Isla during cruises in 2025He said passengers were initially offered a 15% refund due to the air conditioning problems, which was increased to 40% when the cruise was cut short on the penultimate day.But he thinks the holiday should not have gone ahead in the first place."Had I known that the air conditioning wasn't working, having gone on river cruises before, I wouldn't have gone," he said.Problems with the Isla have continued this year.John Welsh, who boarded in June, said some toilets were out-of-order and also reported issues with air conditioning."The whole ship was a sweat box," he said, with some passengers in cabins that had no windows resorting to sleeping on the ship's roof.Welsh said staff were "soaking to the skin with sweat working in the restaurant", and he also needed to change his sweat-soaked clothes after eating there.He said he felt "fobbed off" when he complained to the cruise director. He accepted TUI's offer of a Â£140 per person refund for the problems with the air conditioning but said he would never travel with the company again.'Indefensible'Image source,Getty ImagesImage caption,Water levels on the Danube River in Budapest reached record lows this yearBy July, low river levels due to the heatwave were severely affecting European cruises.Tony Harper was informed a few days before his trip began on 20 July there would be some coach travel in place of sailing.But issues with the ship itself also stood out."The common area smelt of sewage, there was water dripping through the ceiling and there were public toilets out of action for the whole voyage," he said.And there were portable air conditioning units onboard, which he said were not effective.Harper said: "You can't hold it against them for the low river, that's just nature."But it was the way they dealt with that. It was their communication and poor maintenance of the ships, and you can't put it down to anything else other than that."It's indefensible, really."TUI River Cruises said it had experienced "unexpected technical issues affecting air conditioning systems" as well as other challenges caused by low water levels on the Danube.It said extreme heat across parts of Europe had put systems under pressure and extensive repairs and maintenance work had been undertaken, including temporary measures.The company added that it was investing in its air conditioning systems across its European river cruise fleet this winter, including significant upgrades.Related topicsTUI GroupTravelCruise shipsMore on this storyCruise passengers 'stranded' after air con failure to be flown homePublished30 June

title: 美光首席执行官：人工智能“彻底改变”了内存行业的繁荣与萧条
content:
美光科技首席执行官桑杰·梅赫罗特拉 (Sanjay Mehrotra) 周四表示，人工智能从根本上改变了内存行业，这个行业容易出现繁荣与萧条周期。

“今天，没有内存就没有人工智能。人工智能系统需要更多内存。它们需要更高性能的内存。它们需要更低功耗的内存，”Mehrotra 在“Mad Money”节目中对 Jim Cramer 说道。 “所以，存储器的价值，这个等式已经完全改变了。”

他的评论是在美光爱达荷州博伊西总部附近正在建设的大型半导体制造厂的阴影下进行的，这是该公司计划在美国制造和研究投资 2500 亿美元的一部分。博伊西工厂最终将包括两个工厂，每个工厂大约有 10 个足球场大小；据梅赫罗特拉称，单个工厂的钢筋数量足以绕地球两圈。第一家博伊西晶圆厂预计将于 2027 年中期开始生产晶圆。这项投资的规模反映了 Mehrotra 认为人工智能如何极大地改变了存储器的前景。

存储器历来是一个周期性行业，需求旺盛的时期会鼓励制造商增加产能，但供应过剩最终会压低价格。然而，Mehrotra 是一位在芯片行业工作了 40 多年的工程师，之前是 SanDisk 的联合创始人，他表示人工智能正在创造更持久的需求来源。

他说，这个机会不仅限于数据中心。 Mehrotra 表示，他预计未来几年自动驾驶汽车、机器人和支持人工智能的消费设备将需要越来越多的内存。

“今天的内存至关重要，”Mehrotra 说。 “这就是为什么我将其称为人工智能时代的战略基础设施。”

Mehrotra 表示，这种需求也正在改变客户对内存的重视。他表示，客户不能简单地招标并从价格最低的供应商处购买，而是必须越来越多地与内存运行的处理器和系统一起设计。 Mehrotra 表示，这使得内存对于更广泛系统的性能至关重要，而不仅仅是另一个组件。

“我们在他们的开发周期中越来越早地与他们密切合作，”他说。 “我们的客户认识到内存的价值，因为内存使他们能够设计出能够推动其增长引擎的产品。”

他表示，美光仍然无法生产足够的产品来满足这一需求。

Mehrotra 表示：“我们终端市场上的所有客户都会购买我们生产的所有产品。”他补充说，数据中心客户目前希望比美光能够承诺的供应多大约 50%。

这家内存制造商正在通过以下方式更深入地了解这一需求：长期客户协议，对于历史上受到现货市场波动影响的企业来说，这是另一个重要转变。在该公司 6 月底举行的最近一次财报电话会议上，美光宣布已与 16 家客户签署了为期五年的战略协议。 Mehrotra 表示，该公司此后签署了更多协议。

“他们已承诺接受供应，”Mehrotra 说。 “因此，这为我们提供了需求保证。”

title: 洛杉矶湖人队以 125 亿美元的价格出售。这是现在每支 NBA 球队的身价
content:
洛杉矶湖人队的破纪录出售远远超出了好莱坞的范围。

马克·沃尔特 (Mark Walter) 即将以 125 亿美元的价格出售给约书亚·库什纳 (Joshua Kushner) 和鲍勃·艾格 (Bob Iger) 将对所有 NBA 球队的估值产生重大影响。

根据 CNBC 自营球队交易，如果出售获得批准，NBA 球队的平均价值将增加 21% 至 66.8 亿美元

10月，沃尔特以100亿美元的估值购买了湖人队的控股权。这笔 125 亿美元的交易预计将是球队 2025-26 赛季收入的 20 倍，这是 NBA 球队控股权的历史最高倍数。

CNBC 根据湖人队 125 亿美元的交易调整了 2 月份发布的所有 30 支球队的 NBA 估值。

金州勇士队仍将是最有价值的球队，但其价值将从 130 亿美元增加到 130 亿美元。 2 月份为 108 亿美元。与 2 月份相比，价值增幅最大的两支球队是 NBA 卫冕冠军纽约尼克斯队和芝加哥公牛队，各自上涨了 26%。

除了历史销售价格及其相应的收入倍数之外，CNBC 在我们的估值中考虑的因素还包括球馆经济、市场规模和投资者兴趣。

title: 迄今为止，贝森特在国债市场的努力尚未奏效。这是他还可以尝试的其他方法
content:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent insisted Thursday that he has multiple weapons at his disposal to quell liquidity problems in the government debt market and restore calm.

While that's true in itself, a two-pronged effort he has deployed so far — accelerated buybacks and an effort to talk the market into accepting the rationale — have met with little success.

The Treasury announcement Wednesday that it would at leastdouble its bond buybacksstarting in early September sent yields tumbling as investors applauded a backstop for longer-maturity government bonds.

However, yields at the long endquickly rose again Thursdayas market experts showed skepticism at whether the push would succeed against a bevy of factors working against Treasurys.

Then on Thursday, Bessent appeared on CNBC with assurances that the intervention was merely aimed at providing market liquidity and not at trying to control the yield curve. While yields initially nudged lower, they quickly rebounded amid criticism of how the prior day's announcement was rolled out, leading one analyst to characterize the appearance as having "minimal impact" on the market pressures.

Still, that leaves Bessent with a variety of options that he may yet choose to deploy.

"We have a big toolkit," the Treasury chief said. "Part of it is signaling here and to show that we believe that the yields don't reflect the underlying fundamentals."

Yet markets are still worried, and criticism rose that the size of the buybacks, which Bessent confirmed could exceed $4 billion, would be rendered ineffective in such a large market.

Evercore ISI analyst Krishna Guha called the plan "a weak form of Operation Twist," or a Federal Reserve initiative that swaps longer-term notes and bonds for short-term bills. The move "in itself will have little enduring impact and could backfire if it is seen as signaling concern about the ability to fund longer-term at acceptable cost," he said. The interview "had minimal impact on the bond market," he added.

That leaves Bessent with a handful of other options, none guaranteed to work and each carrying its own risk:

Whichever route he chooses — and he could also choose to do nothing and let the markets sort it out — Bessent could face credibility challenges from a market already growing skeptical and leery of the challenges Treasurys are facing.

Jefferies' chief U.S. economist Thomas Simons complained that the buyback announcement itself was improper. He pointed out that the move came two weeks after Treasury announced its quarterly refunding plans, during which it gave no indication that it was considering changing the buyback scheme.

"This breaks with Treasury's long-held strategy of making 'regular and predictable' announcements, and using the Refunding to announce almost all of their policy changes and guidance," Simons wrote. "We do not think it is hyperbole to say that this break in communication strategy reduces the overall credibility of their guidance."

Moreover, Simons added that "the sloppy wording of [the] headline on [the] release gave the impression that this was a hastily made decision."

The challenge, then, for Bessent could be that efforts to suppress longer-end yields could give investors another reason to demand more compensation.

Along the lines of what Bessent told CNBC on Thursday, not all of the factors at play are fundamental. They include rising competition from corporate bond issuance as well as suddenly attractive yields of other sovereigns including Japan; a correlation with oil prices that in turn increases inflation fears; and increasing term premiums, or the extra yield investors are demanding.

To combat those problems, Bessent could seek cooperation with the Federal Reserve. Though Fed ChairmanKevin Warshhas stressed the importance of letting the market set rates, Bessent suggested Thursday that the two entities "would work together" in dealing with complications in the bond markets and as the central bank manages its own Treasury holdings.

The various moving parts come during a paradigm shift in the government debt markets, both in the U.S. and globally.

"There has also been a structural shift in who buys U.S. government debt," said Atsi Sheth, chief credit officer at Moody's Ratings. "As central banks shrink their balance sheets and traditional duration buyers reach the limits of how much additional issuance they can absorb, new buyers, such as leveraged hedge funds running relative-value strategies, are playing a bigger role."

On top of all that, the U.S. faces a daunting fiscal situation in the form of adeficit-to-GDP ratioof nearly 6%, or about triple its average from the end of World War II until the Covid pandemic. That is compounding a problem with thenational debt, which just surpassed $40 trillion.

With PresidentDonald Trumphungry for tax cuts and Congress showing few signs of spending restraint, the fiscal problems are likely to mount. To that end, Bessent said he and Russell Vought, head of the Office of Management and Budget, will meet soon to discuss "fiscal consolidation," generally understood to refer to efforts to reduce red ink.

"It's that combination of the deficits, the borrowing needs, inflation expectations, not really knowing what future Fed policy is going to be, and the sustainability of being able to issue higher, ever higher, levels of U.S. Treasury debt, and what rates those need to be at," said JoAnne Bianco, senior investment strategist at BondBloxx. "There's just the idea that there needs to be a higher risk premium for all the issuance."

title: 随着贝森特进军央行地盘，沃什面临美联储独立性考验
content:
If Treasury SecretaryScott Bessenttruly wants to bring the full force of the federal government to bear on what he sees as a misbehaving bond market, he can't go it alone. A sustained effort to bring down Treasury yields would eventually require coordination with Bessent's longtime friend, now at theFederal Reserve, ChairmanKevin Warsh.

Bessent's efforts to influence the bond market will add to the immense scrutiny on Warsh to clarify where he stands on theFed's independenceand on its attitude about the vast pool of U.S. government debt.

The Fed has historically only intervened in the bond market to affect yields in periods of severe economic weakness or clear emergencies. The concerns Bessent has expressed so far fall below that threshold, and there is no sign the central bank intends to get involved now. But there is no definitive line between where Treasury's responsibilities end and the Fed's begin, and Warsh has said repeatedly that he believes the Fed ought to hand more power to the Treasury over sensitive matters involving the Fed'sbalance sheet.

The Treasury Departmenton Wednesdayannounced it would buy back at least $2 billion worth of long-dated treasuries on top of its existing plans. That would need to be offset by shorter-maturity debt.

Bessent suggested he might have more plans in store. "We have a big toolkit, so we'll see," Bessentsaid on CNBCThursday.

"Part of it is signaling here and to show that we believe that the yields don't reflect the underlying fundamentals," Bessent said. Yields on the10-year Treasurynote dropped on Wednesday, but had already unwound most of those gains on Thursday.

"There's more firepower in terms of how you manage the yield curve sitting at the Federal Reserve," Rick Rieder, chief investment officer of global fixed income, told CNBC Wednesday.

"Going to Jackson Hole, that's going to be interesting to see how they address that," Rieder said.

Warsh was already facing questions about his relationship to the Treasury market going into the Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium, the annual late-August gathering of central bankers in the Wyoming mountains.

Warsh's remarks after the FOMC's July meeting gave some in the markets the impression thathe welcomed a rise in long-term bond yields.

Bond traders raised yields further to account for that uncertainty, said Loretta Mester, former president of the Cleveland Fed.

"I think part of what's happening is we don't have very much clarity yet on what Kevin Warsh's plans are," Mestersaidin an interview on CNBC. "We don't even have clarity on their reaction function."

Warsh in July said he was concerned about inflation, but didn't directly answer reporters' questions about what it would take for him to raise interest rates to address it.

Warsh has also been vague on the precise limits of the Fed's authority over certain aspects of the financial system.

"Fed independence is at its peak in the conduct of monetary policy," Warsh said at his Senate confirmation hearing in April. That nuanced view implies that some aspects of the Fed's operations aren't fully independent. Warsh carved out bank supervision as an example of non-independent policy, but he hasn't fully specified exactly what is and isn't included.

Warsh has separately said he wants the Fed to rewrite its relationship with the Treasury. He proposed in 2025 to update the 1951 Treasury-Fed Accord, which established the modern basis for the division of responsibilities between the two agencies — and secured the Fed's political independence. As part of that revised accord, Warsh wanted to give the Treasury more authority over any major adjustment to the Fed's vast balance sheet.

"The Treasury secretary would need to find the proposed change in Fed holdings acceptable, given that it is partially fiscal policy in disguise,"Warsh said in 2025.

How the Fed thinks about the$6.7 trillionin financial assets currently on its balance sheet could make or break Bessent's plans. Warsh's existing plans would seem to cut against Bessent's hopes to tamp down yields. Warsh wants the Fed to reduce its overall holdings and shift them toward short-term debt, which would likely push up the yield on longer-term Treasuries — the opposite of what Bessent wants to achieve.

But the Fed is divided even on that question. Recently releasedminutes from the Federal Open Market Committee's July meetingshowed that the Fed deferred questions about its balance sheet until a task force Warsh has assigned to report on that issue comes back. That will be late this year or early next.

The Treasury and Fed have in practice historically communicated with each other on major changes in the balance sheet. Bessent on Thursday in an interview on CNBC suggested that would continue.

"I think that the Treasury and the Fed would work together if there was any change in the balance sheet, and we would adjust to any kind of runoff that they're doing," Bessent said.

Neither the Fed nor the Treasury Department responded to emailed questions about whether Bessent's comment implied he and Warsh had begun to coordinate.

title: 现代汽车首席执行官告诉 CNBC，现代汽车将增加佐治亚州新工厂在美国的产量
content:
旧金山 – 现代汽车首席执行官何塞·穆尼奥斯 (José Muñoz) 周四告诉 CNBC，现代汽车计划进一步扩大其位于佐治亚州价值数十亿美元的新汽车装配厂的美国产量。

穆尼奥斯表示，这家韩国汽车制造商预计将其现代汽车集团 Metaplant America 的计划产能从 50 万辆增加到 70 万辆到 2028 年产量将达到 80 万辆。

“对我们来说，除了我们的总部韩国之外，美国是世界上最重要的市场，”穆尼奥斯周四在公司旗舰 Genesis GV90 SUV 发布后接受独家采访时表示。

之前未披露的产能增加是现代汽车计划到 2028 年在美国投资 260 亿美元的一部分。该公司计划推出数十种新产品，并计划在美国国内生产至少 80% 的汽车，高于 2024 年的约 40%。

这些计划可能会使该工厂成为美国产能最大的汽车组装工厂，超过特斯拉和丰田汽车等公司的其他工厂。

现代汽车还在评估对佐治亚州 Meta 工厂以外产能的额外投资。 ” “好消息是，我们在宣布关税之前就已经开始行动了。因此，在某种程度上，这有助于我们加速发展。”

现代汽车最初于 2022 年宣布了该工厂的建设计划，但该公司仍在继续扩大其投资 76 亿美元的工厂的计划，该工厂旨在为现代汽车、Genesis 及其兄弟企业起亚生产混合动力和全电动汽车。

Metaplant 目前生产全电动现代 Ioniq 5 和Ioniq 9 以及起亚 Sportage 混合动力车。

Muñoz 去年上任时成为该汽车制造商第一位非韩国首席执行官，他表示该公司的计划包括在该工厂生产各种不同的车辆，并雇用数千人。目前的 500,000 辆汽车计划包括佐治亚大型工厂的 8,500 多名员工以及场外供应商的 6,900 名员工。

现代汽车在这十年中在美国的销量实现了大幅增长，甚至在 Metaplant 上线之前也是如此。根据公司报告和 Mobility Global 的数据，该品牌及其母公司（包括起亚和 Genesis）的销售额增长了近 50%。

根据 Mobility Global（前身为 S&P Global Mobility）的数据，现代汽车在美国的市场份额从 2020 年的 8.4% 增加到去年的 11.2%。

title: 由于美国购物者减少，沃尔玛销售面临压力
content: 图片来源，盖蒂图片社 图片说明，伊利诺伊州芝加哥市的一家沃尔玛。弗朗西斯科·韦拉斯克斯商业记者报道，纽约发布 25 分钟前 美国零售巨头沃尔玛最近一个季度的销售额增长速度为六年多以来最慢，这表明美国购物者面临压力。沃尔玛因其规模而能够很好地衡量消费者的情绪，因此将其归咎于燃油价格上涨。该公司表示，5月至7月期间，不包括燃料在内的环比上涨了2.6%。沃尔玛表示，将使用高达30亿美元的预期关税退款来降低价格，以保持顾客消费。这笔退款源于特朗普总统去年对进口商品征收一波关税后零售商支付的关税。这些关税被裁定为非法后，零售商正在从中央政府获得退款。竞争对手零售商 Target 最近表示，它已收到 10 亿美元的退税，从而提高了利润。美国最大的零售商沃尔玛表示，预计近 30 亿美元的关税退税将有助于其继续今年早些时候扩大的降价或“回滚”计划（外部）。沃尔玛严重依赖降价来留住客户，推出了其所谓的跨品类“回滚”商品中有 11,000 件。首席财务官约翰·大卫·雷尼 (John David Rainey) 表示，价格下跌已经提升了交易量和销量，尤其是食品和玩具等其他主食。但他承认，零售环境仍然不平衡，低收入家庭（沃尔玛基础的核心部分）感到受到挤压。雷尼表示，汽油价格上涨导致购物者的闲置现金减少，并表示一旦燃油价格上涨，行为的转变就会变得明显。每加仑 4 美元。他补充说，6 月份的价格变动带来的影响显而易见，低收入客户开始减少支出，将支出集中在必需品上。除了消费者回落之外，沃尔玛的业绩还凸显了可能影响该公司未来几个月前景的几个额外风险。该季度的利润增长大部分来自已经收到的关税退款，分析师称这种一次性收益不会达到同样程度。价格回落可能会给利润率带来压力，而沃尔玛也在自动化、新仓库和技术升级上投入资金。在财报电话会议上，分析师向管理层施压，询问较低的价格是否已经推动了销售额的增长，以及是否可以在 2027 年锁定一些回滚。沃尔玛表示，这些好处在食品和其他主食上表现得最为明显，如果它们继续引起购物者的共鸣，那么某些削减可能会继续存在。“我们的希望和意图始终是，回滚可以成为永久性的......只要有可能，”雷尼说。分析师还质疑是否可以这样做。尽管销售额低迷，沃尔玛的收入仍可能继续增长。高管们表示他们相信可以做到这一点，并指出会员和广告等业务。相关主题沃尔玛零售生活成本公司

title: Gatekeeping bots, piles of slop: Welcome to the age of AI weirdness at work
content:
Somewhere in Chicago, one 40-year-old project director spent her summer wondering if she's been working with a human or a bot.

She was recently put on a project with an artificial intelligence expert who started using AI agents to manage his inbox. But in the course of their partnership, the bots began filtering out important emails and texts, leading to delays delivering on promises to their client and no other way to reach him, the project director tells CNBC Make It.

Now, despite previously being in touch over phone and video calls, she says her team can't reach the AI expert to honor their contract and pay him for the finished work. "I actually looked up their local speaking engagements to see if I could just go maybe meet them," the project director says. At this point, she's second-guessing whether he's even a real human.

"I will take a messy human over a robot any day," she says. "How do I get through to a machine?"

Welcome to the age of AI weirdness at work.

AI isreshaping jobs,businessesand, iftech bosses' predictions come true, the future ofthe entire workforce. Talks of an uncertain AI-powered future aside, the developing tech is also creating a mess of how humans interact in the workplace right now. People arepassing off workslopto their colleagues, accusing each other of lazy AI use, picking fights over who's smarter than AI and punting questions from their direct reports.

For this article, CNBC Make It reached out to over a dozen employees and business leaders to take a closer look at the frustration brewing among workers, some of whom declined to be identified for fear of professional repercussions. The picture that unfolds is messy, awkward and, in the case of the missing AI expert, downright strange.

Since generative AI burst onto the scene in 2022 with the public launch of ChatGPT, people have generally been left to their own devices to experiment with AI.

Today, roughly half of workers say they use AI anywhere from once a week up to multiple times per day, according totheCNBC and SurveyMonkey Quarterly AI and Jobs Surveypublished Thursday. However a majority, 84%, of people say they're self-taught with no formal training in AI, and 55% say their workplace doesn't have an official AI policy, per the survey of 1,686 workers.

Workers are getting mixed messages from every direction of their orgs about how, when and why to AI: Their boss may encourage them to use it to work faster, better and smarter, while peers side-eye them for taking a shortcut or question whether they're actually doing the work.

That was Joanna Briggs' concern when a colleague complimented an email the 30-year-old HR worker in London had sent, then immediately followed up by asking whether she'd used ChatGPT on it.

Briggs, who says she researched and crafted the message without the help of AI, took it as a backhanded compliment. "It kind of just puts your back up a bit, and you think, 'No, I really worked on this,' and you want the credit. You want your skill to be recognized," she says, adding that her snap response came from feeling like her hard-earned skills were reduced to being able to prompt an AI tool reasonably well.

Assumptions like the one that made Briggs bristle can carry big penalties: People were perceived as lazier and less likely to be put up for big projects if they said they used AI in their work, according to oneAtlassian experimentinvolving 1,000 U.S. workers.

One 26-year-old copywriter in Chicago laments that her job has been reduced to editing her coworkers' AI writing and challenging what they copy from a chatbot.

She once felt comfortable sharing critiques of their work, like if the writing wasn't clear. "Now that people have access to something that they see as this like all-knowing CEO of writing, they feel more emboldened to push back" on her revisions.

"Don't get me wrong, I am not an expert [or] the primary authority on all things correct writing," she says. In the past, she would have heard her colleagues out on their opinions. Now she questions: "Is that what you believe, or is that what Claude told you?"

Then there are the workers fuming at colleagues for making their jobs harder with piles of slop.

Some 40% of U.S. desk workers said they receivedworkslop, or AI-generated content that looked good but lacked substance, leading to additional hours of work to fix errors and a potential multi-million dollar business productivity hit,according to researchfrom BetterUp and the Stanford Social Media Lab conducted in September 2025.

Kim Bode, founder and CEO of a Grand Rapids, Michigan-based communications company called 8thirtyfour, says she lost $10,000 when she hired a contractor to work on a campaign. She says she had to "rewrite every single piece of content" because what she received appeared to be "clearly generated by AI."

"The quality of work has significantly decreased" due to AI, and it's "very much straining relationships," says Bode, 47.

Other than being an annoying time-suck, workslop is leading people to question their coworkers' competence or consideration.

"It's hard to tell whether or not they think it's actually good and satisfactory, or if they're like, 'I know it's not good, but I'm going to send it over anyways,'" says one 20-something marketer from the Midwest. "I'll get really upset, and I'm like, 'Are they doing it on purpose or not? Do they actually think this is fine?' Both are problematic in their own ways."

The behavior makes her slower to respond to some requests, she says. "I just know it's going to be more work, and I'm like, I just don't even have the mental space to deal with this right now."

AI's rise at work is putting many workers on edge: Roughly 1 in 5 workers say it makes them feel like their job is less secure, and some 1 in 3 are more pessimistic about the current job market because of it, according to the CNBC survey.

Worker anxiety has been simmering for months in the currentlow-hire, low-fire job market, where people are eitherclinging to their jobs,searching for months on endwithout success ordropping out of the workforceentirely while AI looms as anever-growing threat for layoffs.

Meanwhile, businesses are directing workers to move faster and see AI as the solution to do so, oftentimes leaving individuals with the task of figuring out how AI will save them time and money, says Leena Rinne, vice president of product portfolio at Skillsoft, a Nashua, New Hampshire-based skills management company. That can put workers in a stressful situation: "Everyone needs to do everything now — more with less," she says.

So far the resultshave been mixed: AMay reportfrom the tech research firm Gartner found businesses that laid off workers in favor of AI spending did not see a return on investment. And an often-cited2025 reportfrom Massachusetts Institute of Technology researchers found that 95% of organizations saw zero return on their $30 billion to $40 billion investment into generative AI.

The pressure to perform, from boards of directors to executives to managers and their teams, could lead to people leveraging "AI just for the sake of using AI," says Victor Riparbelli, co-founder and CEO of Synthesia, a London-based AI video platform. Earlier this year, Riparbelli says he had tocall out his own stafffor using AI to create overcomplicated written documents that amounted to little but fluff.

AI tools like Claude or ChatGPT can prop users up as "the world's most articulate person," Riparbelli says, but upon closer inspection, "sometimes it's just a lot of filler" that others then have to decipher.

Some workers are using AI as a "middleman" to interact with their human colleagues. The disconnect between intent and impact could be sowing discord.

Roughly 1 in 4 workers who use AI have redirected a colleague to ask AI before coming to them, according to the CNBC survey; the top reasons they cited for punting were to encourage their colleague to be more self-sufficient as well as to save time and avoid interruptions.

These redirects, however well-intended, may miss the point. "It feels really lazy and sloppy to people" and "borderline insulting," says Alison Green, the former chief of staff turned management consultant and creator of the Ask a Manager advice column. "It's almost like sending Google results to someone. You're perfectly capable of feeding it into AI yourself if you want to. The reason you're asking them is because you're looking for their particular expertise."

Resorting to AI to save time at the expense of human interaction can hamper creativity and innovation, says Jennifer Birdsall, chief clinical officer at ComPsych, an employee assistance programs provider. "Human connection — it's not the opposite of productivity," she says.

Social offloading from bosses, who are bothmore enthusiasticabout andmore likelyto use AI at work compared with individual contributors, can crush teams. When leaders use AI as a substitute for developmental conversations, like for mentorship or career advice, workers' desire to quit increases by 29%, burnout rises by 26%, and team coordination drops by 12%, according toresearchconducted by BetterUp Labs, Stanford Social Media Lab and Saïd Business School at Oxford University that was released in April.

"There's a psychological cost if everything is mediated through AI," says Rinne of Skillsoft.

Figuring out how to use new tech leaves plenty of room for potential gaffes.

title: 贝森特表示，特朗普领导下的美国预算赤字“很有可能”已见顶
content:
美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特 (Scott Bessent) 周四表示，唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Trump) 总统领导下的美国预算赤字“很有可能”已见顶。

在财政部宣布非凡的债务回购计划后一天，贝森特在接受 CNBC 记者萨拉·艾森 (Sara Eisen) 独家采访时表示，“我们将高度集中精力”。

美国月度预算赤字达到顶峰美国财政部上周表示，7 月份的支出为 4,320 亿美元，为 50 多年来的最高水平。该月度报告显示，本财年迄今为止的赤字攀升至近 1.8 万亿美元，高于一年前的同期水平。

财政部本周宣布，美国政府为赤字提供资金的债务规模再创新高，超过 40 万亿美元。债务总额在过去十年中增加了一倍多，加剧了人们对国家金融健康状况的担忧。

贝森特本人、特朗普和美国财政部董事拉塞尔·沃特 (Russell Vought) 表示，管理和预算办公室是致力于财政整顿措施的联邦政府领导人之一。贝森特说，通过这些努力可以节省数千亿美元。

白宫将其对贸易伙伴征收广泛而严格的关税的目标宣传为收入的驱动因素，有助于减少国家债务。但这些征税一再遇到法律障碍，最明显的是最高法院决定取消其中许多征税。

然而贝森特表示，他预计今年的关税收入将在尽管面临挑战，但重新实施征税后，仍与 2025 年的水平相同。他说，这次这些收入不应该退还给公司。

“40 万亿的数字并没有什么神奇之处，”贝森特说。 “我们可以通过自己的方式摆脱困境。”

title: 由于财政部计划未能压低收益率，道指下跌近 500 点，沃尔玛大跌：实时更新
content:
U.S. stocks fell on Thursday asTreasury yields reversed coursefrom the decline seen in the prior trading day after the Treasury Department'sdebt buyback announcement.

TheDow Jones Industrial Averageshed 460 points, or 0.9%. TheS&P 500lost 0.4%, while theNasdaq Compositedropped 0.9%.

Bond yields advanced on Thursday, climbing back from Wednesday's slide following the Treasury Department saying it will at least double repurchases of 10-, 20- and 30-year debt in the next few months. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessenttold CNBCThursday that the debt buyback operation could actually be larger than the $4 billion that was announced.

The30-year Treasurybond yield added more than 5 basis points at 5.251%, while the yield on the10-year Treasurynote gained more than 5 basis points to 4.706%%. The 30-year yield spiked to its highest level in nearly 20 years earlier this week.

Adam Phillips, managing director of investments at EP Wealth Advisors, is skeptical that the buyback program will be enough to provide any relief, however.

"This is not the cure to what ails the bond market. There are structural forces here at play that are really beyond the Treasury and the administration's control," he said, adding that the relief seen in the wake of past interventions have generally been short-lived. "You're going to need to come at it with a little bit more force if it's going to have staying power."

Also weighing on equities, oil pricesrose againamid increasing tensions between Iran and the U.S. When discussing Iran, PresidentDonald Trumpsaid in a Truth Social postWednesday that the U.S. would begin the "MOST CRUSHING ECONOMIC OPERATION EVER TAKEN AGAINST ANY COUNTRY!"

"This will be Economic Warfare and Isolation on an unprecedented scale," he wrote.

On that front, Bessent said in a Thursday interview with CNBC that the U.S. is going to impose the "toughest sanctions in history" against Iran.

West Texas Intermediate crude futuresrose 2% to trade above $88 per barrel, while global benchmarkBrent crude futuresmoved up 2% to above $93 a barrel.

A pullback inWalmartshares hit the broader market as well. The retail giant dropped 9% after its U.S. comparable sales missed analyst expectations, as did its adjusted earnings forecast for both the third quarter and full year.

Wall Street is coming off a winning session, with the S&P 500 snapping a three-session losing streak, as yields on longer-dated U.S. Treasurys pulled back from multi-year highs after the government unveiled a plan to ease pressure from a recent bond market rout.

— CNBC's Tobias Burns contributed reporting.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC on Thursday that an accelerated buyback of government debt could be higher than the announced $4 billion.

In a live interview, Bessent said his department is going "make a market" in the longer-dated securities where yields have been surging lately. Treasury announced Wednesday that it would be doubling its scheduled $2 billion in buybacks of longer-dated government debt, sending yields sharply lower.

"We're going to increase the size of the buyback," he said. "I would note that it could be more than the 4 billion per issue."Read more.

TD Cowen put a hold rating on pharmaceuticals giant Merck despite Wednesday's news that the company's cancer vaccine succeeded in a large trial.

"Success is not unduly surprising given strong Phase II data," Steve Scala at TD Cowen wrote in a Thursday note to clients. "Positive results serve as validation ... but breadth of potential still unknown."

TD Cowen has a price target of $137 on Merck stock, compared to Wednesday closing price of $152.20.

The three major averages began Thursday's session in the red.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 421 points, or 0.8%, just after 9:30 a.m. ET. The S&P 500 dropped 0.4%, while the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.5%.

Factory activity in the Philadelphia area hit its highest level in more than five years during August, the regional Federal Reserve reported Thursday.

The Philadelphia Fed'smanufacturing indexjumped to 47.4, up 6 points from July and well ahead of the Dow Jones consensus forecast for 25. This was the highest reading since April 2021. The index measures the percentage difference between companies reporting expansion against contraction.

The employment index surged to 27.9, up 18 points to its highest level since April 2022. At the same time, gauges for prices paid and received hit their lowest levels since February, just as the U.S. and Israel launched attacks on Iran that sent inflation higher.

Bitcoin'snearly 11% two-day rally on Thursday sent the cryptocurrency above $71,000, as the coin reached its highest levels since June 1.

The move higher came after President Donald Trump along with crypto executives and regulators at the White House made the case for passing the Clarity Act, a cryptocurrency market structure bill, through Congress on Wednesday.

Other coins also hit recent highs.Etherwas at the highest levels since May 12, whileSolanareached levels it hasn't traded at since May 16.

—Nick Wells and Davis Giangiulio

Here are some of the names making moves before the opening bell:

To read the full list of premarket movers, clickhere.

Walmartshares dropped more than 5% in premarket trading after the retail giant's U.S. comparable sales and third-quarter adjusted EPS guidance fell short of FactSet consensus.

For the second quarter, U.S. comparable sales rose 2.6%, below the gain of 3.5% that analysts polled by FactSet had expected. Walmart's third-quarter guidance for adjusted earnings per share was also between $0.62 and $0.64, while analysts had anticipated $0.68.

"Our business model is only getting stronger and more durable, and we're pleased to raise our guidance for the year," said John David Rainey, the company's chief financial officer.

For the third quarter, the company expects net sales to increase 3% to 3.75% and operating income to increase 2% to 4%.

Walmart's guidance for the fiscal year also fell below FactSet's earnings estimate, despite raising its own forecast. The company now expects adjusted EPS of $2.80 to $2.87, up from its previous guidance of $2.75 to $2.85. FactSet consensus was $2.90.

Walmart's second-quarter report also beat FactSet consensus on revenue.

Bond yields edged higheras investors digest the Treasury Department's plan to dramatically ramp up government debt repurchases in a bid to shore up longer-dated debt.

title: 贝森特表示，随着经济压力的加大，美国可能不会重启大规模的伊朗战斗
content:
美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特 (Scott Bessent) 周四对 CNBC 表示，特朗普政府打击伊朗经济的计划可能会导致美国不再需要对伊朗采取进一步的军事行动。

贝森特在接受“Squawk on the Street”独家采访时表示，“如果我们施加最大的经济压力，那么这意味着可能不会出现大规模的经济重启。”

内阁部长的评论就在唐纳德·特朗普总统在《真相社会》上宣布美国计划对任何向德黑兰提供“任何类型的生命线”的国家实施重大经济处罚的几个小时后，美国计划扼杀伊朗的经济。

特朗普在周三晚间的帖子中写道：“这将是一个经济诺曼底登陆日，我们需要我们所有的盟友与美国站在一起，孤立并击败伊朗的威胁。”对伊朗的战争已接近六个月大关，但没有任何迹象表明美国即将取得外交或军事胜利。

贝森特告诉 CNBC，他将于周一召开新闻发布会，“具体讨论我们将要做什么。”

在该计划的预览中，他表示美国将告诉所有盟友，“你们要么支持我们，要么反对我们” ”

“如果你坚持与[伊朗]做生意，无论是转移资金，购买他们的石油还是进行海运船舶转移，那么美国财政部和美国政府......将全力以赴对你采取行动，”贝森特说。

“这将是世界历史上最大的协调经济孤立，”他说。

title: Bessent表示财政部回购操作可能超过40亿美元
content:
财政部长斯科特·贝森特 (Scott Bessent) 周四向 CNBC 表示，加速回购政府债务的规模可能会高于宣布的 40 亿美元。

在现场采访中，贝森特表示，他的部门将在近期收益率飙升的较长期证券上“做市”。财政部周三宣布，将把计划中的 20 亿美元回购规模增加一倍，从而导致收益率大幅下降。

“我们将增加回购规模，”他表示。 “我要指出的是，每期的发行量可能会超过 40 亿美元。”

该言论导致收益率短暂回落，这在很大程度上扭转了周三宣布后的跌势。 30 年期债券最近的交易价格约为 5.235%。所谓的长期债券最近一直处于自 2008 年全球金融危机之前以来的最高水平。

Bessent 讲话时，基准 10 年期债券收益率也短暂回落，但随后走高，最近上涨约 5 个基点至 4.704%。一个基点等于 0.01%。

财政部长指出，收益率水平并未影响回购决策，他希望看到基本面控制市场。

虽然他表示回购可能会增加，但贝森特拒绝附上数字，称这将取决于市场状况。

“我们将看看条件是什么，你知道我们将对其进行分析，”他说。 “我们所做的就是让人们关注基本面，而不是在市场清淡的安静时期进行头条新闻交易。”

Bessent 承认曲线远端的压力，称当前的交易水平并未反映当前的经济状况。

“我们有一个很大的工具包，所以我们会看到，”他说。 “这在一定程度上是在发出信号，表明我们认为收益率没有反映基本面。”

他还将 30 年期债券的流动性描述为“非常差”，这为财政部干预通常强劲的市场提供了另一个动力。

多种因素结合在一起推高了收益率：美国债务和赤字激增；来自其他领域的竞争，包括与人工智能相关的企业债券发行和日本等其他主权国家的更高收益率，以及不断上升的期限溢价，或投资者要求持有政府债务的额外收益。

在财政方面，贝森特表示，他将与管理和预算办公室主任拉塞尔·沃特会面，讨论“财政整顿”。财政部周三公布的数据显示，本周国家债务突破了 40 万亿美元大关。

贝森特表示：“40 万亿美元的数字并没有什么神奇之处，我们可以通过发展摆脱这一困境。”

“我们向我们的盟友、贸易伙伴传达的信息是，全球增长是解决这一巨额债务的出路。”

title: 加州股份公司告诉 CNBC，解决派拉蒙与 WBD 的诉讼需要“强有力的结构性补救措施”
content:
加利福尼亚州总检察长 Rob Bonta 周四对 CNBC 的 David Faber 表示，起诉阻止派拉蒙 Skydance 收购华纳兄弟 Discovery 的州集团需要“强有力的结构性补救措施”才能在反垄断案件中达成和解。

“[派拉蒙]想要谈论一切，除了本案的内容。他们想要谈论流媒体市场，我们对此不要在我们的投诉中指控。他们想谈论 CNN，这不是我们投诉的重点。我们想谈论我们在投诉中提出的三个市场，我们认为这些市场存在反垄断行为。”Bonta 和其他 11 名州总检察长于 7 月提起诉讼，寻求阻止合并。提起诉讼的州还包括亚利桑那州、科罗拉多州、康涅狄格州、马萨诸塞州、明尼苏达州、内华达州、新泽西州、新墨西哥州、纽约州、俄勒冈州和华盛顿州。

派拉蒙最初寻求在 9 月 30 日之前完成交易，但同意将 WBD 的拟议收购推迟到 2027 年 6 月。有关此事的审判将于 3 月份进行。

“我会说，谈判一直是摆在桌面上的事情。如果[首席执行官大卫]埃里森和派拉蒙愿意真诚地坐下来交谈，我们也很高兴进行这样的对话，”邦塔说。 “我们确实更喜欢在董事会而不是法庭上解决案件，但现在我们正在提起诉讼，你知道我希望他们能够关注我们在投诉中提出的实际指控。”

在诉讼中，该集团关注合并后公司的规模以及它将如何控制近三分之一的电影和近三分之一的基本有线电视节目。

如果两家公司合并，它将把著名的电影制片厂华纳兄弟和派拉蒙以及大量电视网络组合，包括派拉蒙的广播网络 CBS 和付费电视频道，例如 MTV 和 BET 以及 WBD 的 CNN、Discovery 等。它还将整合流媒体平台 Paramount+ 和 HBO Max。

title: 从广告到选举，人工智能数据中心的愤怒无处不在
content:
During a brainstorming session earlier this summer, a group of comedians and employees at beverage companyLiquid Deathkicked around an idea for a brazen new advertising campaign that would humorously shed light on the amount of water required to operate massive AI data centers.

"It was an idea of just, hey, what if we used pee to cool data centers instead of water?" Andy Pearson, vice president of creative at Liquid Death, told CNBC in an interview.

The outlandish idea turned into a collaborative90-second video, created with Garage Beer, which is owned by Jason andTravis Kelce. The clip pledges to "send your pee to the AI data center of your choice."

Liquid Death and Garage Beer dropped the video on Tuesday, the same day voters in Florida headed to the polls to vote in the gubernatorial primaries, with the leading Republican candidates focused on data centers as a central issue. Rep. Byron Donalds,President Donald Trump'spick to succeed Gov. Ron DeSantis, won easily to move along to November's general election.

Last month, Donalds introduced the"Protecting Ratepayers Act,"which aims to "ensure that private developers, rather than American taxpayers, bear the investment costs of data center developments that advance our country's technological dominance," according to a release. Donalds, however, received significant financial support from AI PACs like Leading the Future.

The Marc Andreessen-backed group congratulated Donalds after his win, saying he "understands that new, emerging technologies like AI play a key role in advancing that priority.

AI data centers, the large facilities that house the hardware for training and running AI models, are popping up all over the country, with far more coming down the line, if leading AI companies and hyperscalers get their way. But with the midterm elections less than three months away and Americans grappling with increased costs for groceries and stubbornly high prices at the pump, data centers have become a physical manifestation of the widespread antipathy for AI, which consumers associate with inflated electricity bills and job loss.

The National Republican Senatorial Committee (NRSC) warned on Tuesday that data centers have become a "sleeper issue" for the entire midterm election cycle, according to a memo obtained by CNBC. Democrats are currently ahead in the generic ballot by 6.4 percentage points, according to a polling average fromRealClearPolitics.

Pearson said Liquid Death tries to "stay out of political things," but so many people are talking about AI and data centers that it's become a "pretty universal topic." More than half of Americans say they're more concerned than excited about the growing use of the technology in daily life, according toa reportfrom the Pew Research Center published Tuesday. That's up from 37% in 2021.

"You literally can't turn on the TV or radio without hearing about it," Pearson said. "It's really an issue that's uniting people across political and cultural spectrums."

The satirical video Pearson helped produce features former NFL star Jason Kelce, who is shown holding a jar of urine and walking through a field toward a data center singing, "We want your pee, please give us your pee. Let's pee on computers together, to save humanity."

In the NRSC's memo, the committee wrote that data centers have become a fixture of the contentious Senate race in Ohio, where Democratic candidate and former Sen. Sherrod Brown has made his opposition to them a "centerpiece" of his campaign against Republican incumbent Jon Husted.

Ohio is home to several large data center projects, including a massive 10-gigawatt campus in Pike County that could cost more than $500 billion, as CNBCpreviously reported. OpenAIannouncedMonday that it has agreed to secure 8 gigawatts of that capacity, which is backstopped by a$105 billioncommitment fromNvidia.

Ten gigawatts is roughly equivalent to the annual power consumption of8 million U.S. households, according to a CNBC analysis of data from the Energy Information Administration.

"If voters' perceptions of data centers are not fixed quickly, the campaign against them will expand far beyond Ohio," the NRSC wrote in the memo, which was first reported by Axios.

Should Husted lose because of data centers, "the industry will be blamed," and both parties will take notice, the committee wrote. The Ohio race is critical for Republicans in their effort to keep their slim majority in the Senate.

President Trump weighed in on Wednesday, acknowledging that while data centers "can use a little public relations help," communities should welcome them.

"I would absolutely want it because the jobs are enormous and the money paid, the taxes paid, are just enormous," the president said.

A big emerging problem for the tech industry, however, is that voters from both parties disagree. Politicians are responding to their anger.

In Pennsylvania, Democratic Gov.Josh Shapiro, who is eyeing a potential 2028 presidential bid,signed an executive orderon Tuesday placing harsh standards on data center development in his state.

The order requires data center developers to pay for all new electricity generation, transmission, distribution and other infrastructure required for their project. Developers also must commit to open and transparent engagement with local stakeholders, hire and train local workers, enter into "community benefit agreements" and abide by strict water and environmental standards.

Shapiro, who oncewelcomeddata center projects, said he signed the order after hearing from "many residents across our Commonwealth who are concerned about what data center development could mean for our communities, our environment, and our utility bills."

Shapiro's Republican opponent in this year's election, state Treasurer Stacy Garrity, has also seized on data centers as an issue in the campaign, calling for a pause on future development while slamming Shapiro for his earlier positions.

Garrity'scampaign website, which includes a link to "Donate with Crypto," accuses Shapiro of opening "Pennsylvania's door to data centers" and giving away "state tax dollars and resources to a company on the other side of the country."

CNBC reportedin April that the data center boom in Pennsylvania was potentially putting incumbent Republicans in the state at risk.

In Texas, where Republican Gov. Greg Abbott haschampioneddata centers in the past, the mood has changed decisively. Abbott is now racing to put standards on data centers in his state, as Democratic challenger Gina Hinojosa rips him for his initial support of the facilities.

Hinojosa told CNBC on Wednesday that Abbott has been "doing the bidding of the moneyed interests and not the people of Texas." Hinojosa has called for a data center moratorium until the legislature can meet to pass guardrails for them.

Abbott issued adirectivein June to require companies to pay for electrical infrastructure upgrades, reuse their own water and reduce the cost of electricity. On Tuesday, the governorannouncedin a press release that a number of companies agreed to his standards.

AI companies are acutely aware of the souring views toward data centers, and several have made pledges to try and assure Americans that their buildouts will benefit the country.

In January,Microsoftpublisheda blog postoutlining the "concrete steps needed to be a good neighbor in the communities where we build." Days later,OpenAImade a similar pledge, promising to pay its own way on energy while minimizing water use and investing in local jobs and workforce pathways.

"We believe that AIinfrastructure⁠is vital for American competitiveness and economic opportunity, while boosting local economies by creating jobs and bringing in local revenue," OpenAI said ina releaseat the time.

In July, New York Governor Kathy Hochul signed anexecutive orderestablishing the nation's first year-long moratorium on large data centers, effectively pausing the development of new facilities in the state. Hochul said she'll use that time to develop a regulatory framework that better protects the environment, ratepayers, the energy grid and communities in New York.

Trumpattacked the moratoriumin a post onTruth Social, writing that the state should change its policy "IMMEDIATELY."

AnthropicCEO Dario Amodei acknowledged the negative public sentiment around AI ina post on Xon Saturday. He suggested that it stems from a fundamental "crisis of trust" towards the tech industry.

"I think that ordinary people don't trust companies, governments, or the tech industry and always suspect that we are cooking up some new way to screw them over," Amodei wrote. "The causes of this go back decades and AI is just the latest iteration of it."

title: 特朗普和加密货币高管为《澄清法案》做出最后努力，比特币两天内飙升 11%
content:
比特币交易价格达到 6 月以来的最高水平，这在很大程度上要归功于白宫和加​​密货币行业领导者为在未来几周内完成《澄清法案》而做出的最后努力。

比特币价格周四上涨超过 5%，至略低于 72,000 美元，为 6 月 1 日以来的最高水平。此举使其两天涨幅超过 11%。本周早些时候，其交易价格为 63,000 美元。

加密货币股票也紧随其后，周四盘前交易中 Coinbase 和 Circleup 各上涨 6% 左右，Strategy 在前一交易日反弹的基础上上涨超过 9%。

周三，美国国债收益率大幅回落，缓解了风险资产的压力，反弹开始。据 CoinGlass 称，这引发了一场更广泛的加密货币运动，后来又因大规模的空头挤压而放大，大约 27 亿美元的加密货币空头头寸被清算。

同一天，白宫在最后一刻接待了包括 Coinbase、Kraken、Robinhood、Ripple 和 ChainLink 在内的领先加密货币公司的首席执行官，唐纳德·特朗普总统在会上敦促国会在年底前通过被称为《澄清法案》的加密货币市场结构法案的“公平版本”今年的。这次会议是在商品期货交易委员会周四举行的首次创新咨询委员会会议之前举行的。

“我们需要国会采取下一步行动，通过《澄清法案》——公平版本的《澄清法案》，”特朗普在开场白中表示。 “这是一项非常非常强大的结构化立法，它将让我们领先于中国，让我们领先于其他所有人，将为下一波创新和创新者打开大门。”

特朗普对“公平版本”的呼吁反映了民主党的症结所在，他们推动了更严格的道德规则，以防止总统和其他公职人员个人从加密货币中获利，而共和党则抵制他们认为过于有针对性或不公平的条款。限制性的。

《澄清法案》被广泛视为关键催化剂，可以推动市场走出去年秋天开始的加密货币冬天。参议院未经投票进入 8 月休会期，且有关道德条款和共和党与民主党之间其他分歧的谈判仍悬而未决，投资者已开始认为该法案在 2026 年实际上已经死亡。

参议院于 9 月 15 日进行的第一次程序性投票未能清除一个关键障碍，可能会导致该法案今年的机会实际上终结，因为其他优先事项将在中期选举中抢走焦点。

比特币交易仍在约较 2025 年 10 月高点约 126,000 美元下跌 43%。

content:

截至美国东部时间上午 7:55，国际价格基准布伦特原油期货上涨 2.9%，达到每桶 94.31 美元。早盘交易中，9 月交割的美国西德克萨斯中质原油期货上涨 3.3%，至 88.67 美元。

特朗普在《Truth Social》帖子中表示，他为伊斯兰共和国提供了达成协议的机会。他说：“可悲的是，对他们来说，他们没有接受这一点。”

“因此，今天，我宣布对任何国家采取有史以来最具破坏性的经济行动！这将是前所未有的经济战争和孤立。”

他还威胁说，任何为伊朗提供生命线的国家都将面临“巨大的经济后果”。总统表示，这包括现金转移、货币互换和航运登记。

在海湾国家周二表示遭到伊斯兰共和国的攻击后，阿联酋周三表示将停止与伊朗的所有贸易和金融交易，导致油价上涨。

此举给已经面临美国经济制裁的伊朗带来了进一步的压力，并进一步推动了重新签订停火协议的前景。

title: 专家表示，ChatGPT for Teens 在安全方面取得了重要进展。 “真正的问题是，这些有用吗？”
content:
Meta isfacing allegationsit fostered addictive behavior in teens and children in a legal dispute that could brook the company a$200 billion penalty.OpenAI is making an effort to do better by teens.

On Tuesday, OpenAI releasedChatGPT for Teens, a version of the chatbot geared toward 13- to 17-years-olds that contains more guardrails for young users and additional parental controls.

"Our goal is for teens to use AI responsibly to learn, create and explore," OpenAI spokesperson Eric Porterfield told CNBC Make It over email.

Among the tool's new features are "study mode," which can help teens work through homework or prepare for a quiz, a potential reminder to check for sensitive information before sharing an image and safeguards to "help reduce exposure to sensitive or potentially harmful content," accordingto a postby the San Francisco-based company. Some features must be enabled manually.

"This new teen experience makes some really important safety commitments," saysRobbie Torney, senior director of AI programs at kids' safety nonprofit Common Sense Media. Still, he says, when it comes to these new guardrails, "the real question is, does any of this work?"

Based on previous OpenAI releases and other companies' AI tools, here's what he says parents should keep in mind about ChatGPT for Teens.

Among its features, ChatGPT for Teens will send a safety notification to parents with linked accounts "in limited high-risk situations," for example. What Torney doesn't know is how reliable the system is in identifying those dangers. "If those alerts don't work often enough, or if they don't work fast enough, that could give parents a false sense of security," he says.

Another big question is how easily teens can bypass new guardrails. After three hours of continuous use, ChatGPT for Teens prompts a user to take a break, but it doesn't enforce it, says Porterfield. "We defer to their judgment on whether to step away."

Many of ChatGPT for Teen's new features are education oriented. A majority, 63% of 13-to 17-year-old teens seek an answer for schoolwork from AI rather than working their way through it, according to a Common Sense Mediasurvey of 1,017U.S. teens released on Tuesday.

If a teen is adamant about simply getting the answer from the bot without doing the work, says Torney, "it's really going to be a question of how much does ChatGPT resist or prevent the teen from just getting the answer."

Finally, a major critique of the bot has been itssycophancy, or its flattering and agreeable nature, which experts say encourages engagement.

And though, according to apost by OpenAI, ChatGPT for Teens "should not use romantic language, encourage emotional dependence, or imply that it has feelings or consciousness," the new product allows users to "increase the warmth or the enthusiasm that ChatGPT uses," says Torney. "You can tell it to use more or less emojis." That could still make the product more engaging for teens.

A hot tip for parents: Enable every new feature the bot offers like study hours and quiet hours, says Torney. And remember, in the context of thesenew guardrails, "we don't know how much they work or when they don't work," he says. Don't let them lull you into a false sense of security about what your child is seeing and continue an open line of communication about their use of ChatGPT.

If your teen uses ChatGPT to do their homework, ask if you can peak at a final product like an essay or a math worksheet to see what they're learning, he says.

When it comes to advice for teens, 39% percent say they feel like they're missing out on learning when they use AI, according to the Common Sense Media survey. If you're a young person using the bot, "just be conscious," says Torney. "If you feel like the chatbot is doing more of the heavy lifting, you're probably not getting the educational experience or the learning that you would hope to."

And while ChatGPT and other chatbots are always available, there are benefits that can only come from reaching out to other people, like human connection. Before you turn to a bot for help on any number of things, educational or personal, ask yourself, "am I missing out on the opportunity to connect with my friend, my mom, my grandmother?" says Torney. That opportunity may be far more valuable long-term than just getting an assignment in on time. Ask yourself: "Is this taking away from that time?"

title: 沃尔玛上调全年预期，表示将利用巨额关税退款来保持低价
content:
沃尔玛周四公布的季度销售额超出了华尔街的预期，并上调了今年的预期，因为该公司看到电子商务又一个强劲的季度增长，并受益于关税退款。

“我们的业务很强劲，”首席财务官约翰·大卫·雷尼 (John David Rainey) 告诉 CNBC。 “我们对所取得的进展感到非常满意。”

该零售商表示，随着全球电子商务销售额增长 23%，第二财季收入增长了 5.9%。沃尔玛还表示，美国可比销售额增长了 2.6%，部分被某些药品价格上限生效导致健康和保健业务下降 0.8% 所抵消。 FactSet 的数据显示，这低于华尔街预期的 3.5% 增幅。

沃尔玛表示，预计第三季度净销售额将增长 3% 至 3.75%，调整后每股收益将在 62 美分至 64 美分之间。

该零售商预计今年净销售额将增长 4% 至 5%，而之前的预期为 3.5% 至 4.5%成长。沃尔玛还预计调整后的每股收益将在 2.80 美元至 2.87 美元之间，而之前的指引为每股 2.75 美元至 2.85 美元。

Rainey 告诉 CNBC，该公司有资格获得约 29 亿美元的关税退款，但尚未收回其中不到 1 亿美元。雷尼表示，该公司计划利用这些资金为消费者降低价格，这种影响将在第三季度显现出来。

他补充说，沃尔玛还预计“今年与燃油价格上涨相关的增量成本逆风将超过 20 亿美元”。

沃尔玛努力降低价格之际，许多购物者因感受到高油价和食品成本的压力而削减了支出。由于其价值声誉和作为美国最大零售商的规模，该公司通常能够很好地应对回调。

雷尼表示，沃尔玛继续看到消费者捉襟见肘，尤其是在汽油价格上涨的情况下。他补充道，这正在降低包括牛肉在内的各个类别的价格。

“但消费者仍在消费，实际工资增长也在跟上，因此他们在这种环境下非常有弹性，”雷尼告诉 CNBC。 “但尽管如此，我们还是希望能够进一步降低价格，减少他们的钱包压力。”

根据伦敦证券交易所集团 (LSEG) 对分析师的调查，该公司在第二财季的表现与华尔街的预期相比如下：

截至 7 月 31 日的三个月期间，沃尔玛报告净利润为 63.7 亿美元，即每股 80 美分，而去年同期为 70.3 亿美元，即每股 80 美分。去年同期每股 88 美分。剔除投资损失的影响以及所谓的税务问题带来的收益，沃尔玛公布的调整后每股收益为 81 美分。得益于关税退款优惠，该公司的毛利率增长至 25.4%。

总收入从上年同期的 1,774 亿美元攀升至 1,879.4 亿美元。

在取货和送货、第三方市场和广告等领域的增长推动下，沃尔玛实现了一系列稳健增长。近年来，这家折扣店试图让购物变得更加便捷，并为 Amazon Prime 竞争对手 Walmart+ 会员提供额外福利，从而赢得了高收入客户的市场份额。

沃尔玛表示，公司范围内的会员费收入增长了 17%，Walmart+ 的净增加额创下第二季度新高。美国山姆会员店本季度净销售额为 257 亿美元，同比增长 8.8%，会员费上涨 6%。

与此同时，沃尔玛表示其全球广告收入增长了 38%。

在美国，沃尔玛报告净销售额为 1,252 亿美元，而上年同期为 1,209 亿美元。在国际方面，该公司的净销售额为 352 亿美元，而去年为 312 亿美元。该公司表示，本季度其全球库存增长了 6.7%。

Rainey 表示，库存的很大一部分与更昂贵和高端的品牌有关，因为沃尔玛认为其市场份额增长的最大组成部分来自高收入消费者。

虽然其食品杂货部门出现了中个位数百分点的增长，但健康和保健业务在本季度出现了较低的个位数下降。由于玩具和时装、家具和自有品牌的强势，一般商品收入略有增长。

title: 美光科技斥资 500 亿美元在博伊西扩建项目如何重塑其故乡
content:
Dave Petso has been a wealth manager in Boise, Idaho since the 1980s. His business has survived multiple recessions, the bursting of thedot-com bubbleand the 2008 financial crisis.

For most of Petso's 45-year career,Micron, the hometown maker ofcomputer memory, has been a boring enterprise tech company and, in his words, a "terrible investment."

But almost four years into the artificial intelligence craze, the sleepy semiconductor company is one of the hottest names on the planet, turning many of Petso's clients into sudden millionaires. A big part of Petso's job has become helping Micron employees diversify after a more than tenfold increase in the stock since the end of 2024 lifted the company's market cap past $1 trillion.

"You've got a boatload of money now, and it's all tied up in one company," Petso said in an interview. Where clients had been figuring out what to do with some $20,000 worth of stock, "now we're talking about hundreds of thousands or millions of dollars," he said.

Across Boise, a Mountain West city of about 250,000 residents that's best known for outdoor adventures and the blue turf football field at Boise State University, the Micron boom is showing up in the form of job growth, new construction projects, a bustling dining scene and an influx in new residents.

Micron has broken ground on twonew chip manufacturing facilitiesthat are expected to create more than 17,000 new jobs in the area. That includes 3,500 at Micron, which currently employs about 7,000 people in and around Boise.

With the city's rapid expansion comes plenty of annoyances. Residents complain of frequent traffic jams around town or on Interstate 84, rising housing costs and a rush of people from California and elsewhere altering the local culture and landscape. Average rental prices in Boise have climbed 4.3% in the past year, while average prices nationwide have dropped, according toZillow.

"One of Boise's competitive advantages was our low cost of living," said Jason Crawforth, a lifelong resident of Boise who's been building tech companies in the area for almost 35 years. But Crawforth said that while he's seeing his net worth go up from an investment in Micron, "there's a large demographic of our community that doesn't have a direct benefit from that."

CNBC spoke to residents, business owners, real estate agents and others in the Boise area about the recent boom, its impact on the city and what could still be coming as Micron embarks on a$50 billion expansion plan. They collectively portray the city as an unexpected winner in the global AI buildout, one that's trying to hang onto its identity while not becoming overreliant on a technology with a long history of boom-and-bust cycles.

While the trajectory still points up and to the right,Micron shares plunged 29% in July, their worst month since 2002. Shareholders hope it was just a corrective blip, and not a sign of things to come. The stock is up 14% so far in August.

Micron was founded in Boise nearly 50 years ago in the basement of a dental office. By 1981 its first chip fabrication plant was up and running there, pumping out general-purpose memory chips known as DRAM. In itslatest quarter,DRAM accounted for 76% of Micron's total revenue.

DRAM is also the type of chips that are stacked to make high-bandwidth memory, or HBM, which is then added to the powerful processors used for AI.

As HBM gobbles up the world's supply of DRAM, it's caused a global shortage and skyrocketing memory costs, leading to higher prices across the board, even for consumer electronics likeApple'sMacBooks and iPads.

All three of the world's top HBM suppliers — market leaderSK Hynix, Samsung and Micron — arebuilding huge new plantsto try and meet demand. SK Hynix and Samsung are constructing mega-fabs in their home country of South Korea.

They've all been handsomely rewarded by the stock market despite the July pullback. Micron leads the pack, up almost 670% in the past year, followed by SK Hynix at about 470% and Samsung at over 250%.

The rally turnedMicron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra, a nine-year veteran of the company, into a billionaire earlier this year, though last month's selloff pushed him below that mark.

For Mehrotra, Boise represents a big opportunity to help turn his company into a hotbed for U.S. manufacturing. The first of Micron's two new Boise fabs is scheduled to come online in 2027. It will be the country's first front-end factory for manufacturing leading-edge memory. Most of Micron's top-end memory is currently produced in Taiwan, Japan and Singapore.

The site also includes utility and water-treatment buildings to support the resource-intensive process of making chips. Local utilityIdaho Powertold CNBC in a statement that it "does not expect large-load growth, including Micron's expansion, to increase electric bills for other customers."

Additional AI-driven growth in the area is coming fromMeta, which is building an $800 million data center 20 miles southwest, in Kuna, Idaho, that itsayswill create about 100 operational jobs. There's a flurry of new offices from Micron suppliers likeLam Researchand cleanroom builder Exyte, plus contractors coming in for lucrative jobs helping to build Micron's fabs.

With Boise, and an even bigger memory fab campus coming toClay, New York, Micron's long-term goal is to produce 40% of its DRAM in the U.S. It plans to spend $250 billion through 2035 to get there, with the help of up to $6.2 billion of CHIPS Act funds, which were granted under the Biden administration.

Micron is part of the fabric of Boise's economy, alongside other local legends like theAlbertsonsgrocery chain and the potato empire of J.R. Simplot, who was one of Micron's first investors.

Today, the memory maker is among Ada County's leading employers, after Boise State and the region's health system.

"It's always been something that we've been around, but of course recently, with Boise, Idaho being a very small market, it's probably one of our largest success stories that we've ever had," said JT Belnap, founder of Treasure Valley Financial Planning, which is now almost exclusively focused on managing Micron employees' wealth.

Belnap told CNBC that his firm's phones are "continuing to ring" with requests from Micron employees who are close to retirement.

Because of the stock appreciation, some are moving up their timelines to exit the workforce from three or four years to one or two, Belnap said. To take advantage of tax benefits, others are donating stock to charities. And plenty are taking some profit for a dream purchase, like one of Belnap's clients who recently bought an $80,000 truck he'd always wanted.

"What I've learned doing financial planning for as long as I have is when anyone comes into some real wealth that's kind of a sudden thing, you need to allow them to have a little bit of fun," Belnap said.

About 9 miles east of Belnap's office, a very different kind of business is noticing a similar trend. Lisa Zimowsky, owner of jewelry boutique The Diamond Girls, said her sales are up 60% for the year.

"I do know of several people that have sold some stock and bought with us," Zimowsky said. "Usually it's the people that got a quarterly bonus when the stock was $150," or less than one-sixth its current price.

"The Boise economy is super strong," Zimowsky added. "I think Micron's been a big part of that."

Then there's the real estate market.

Sheila Smith, an agent in the area, said she's seen more prospective buyers and fewer listings for homes in the southeast part of the city, near Micron's headquarters. Smith said there's so much construction that some Micron contractors involved with the new fabs are purchasing homes.

"Typically if somebody knows they're only going to be here temporarily, for an interim-type job, such as the engineers, they don't look to buy," Smith said in an interview. "They are coming here and they are buying."

Mortgage broker Gerald Robinson said that over about a month-long stretch, he consulted with four Micron clients who were looking to buy homes.

"We're seeing a lot of stock options being executed right now, and people [are] purchasing," said Robinson, CEO of 1st Choice Mortgage.

One of the two clients who ended up buying a house did so as an investment to run anAirbnb-style property, Robinson said. The other was a first-time homebuyer in her early 20s.

Two of the prospects didn't end up needing Robinson's help, as they opted to sell stock and buy properties in cash, Robinson said.

Micron told CNBC that stock offerings are a key part of the company's strategy to recruit and retain talent. Through the first three quarters of this fiscal year, Micron hadrecorded$954 million in stock-based compensation, up more than 100% fromthree years ago.

"We do lean into stock awards very heavily," said April Arnzen, Micron's chief people officer and an Idaho native who's worked at the company for 27 years. "We want our team members to be owners in the company and share in the success of the company."

It's not just employees who have gotten in on the action.

As a longtime part of the Boise tech community, Crawforth bought Micron shares when they traded around $16 each, and said he still owns north of 1,500 to this day. That's a stake worth over $1.4 million.

But the growth led to an accidental imbalance in the family.

"I made a mistake – I bought some for my niece, but not for my nephew," Crawforth said. "All of a sudden, my niece's investment to help her put a down payment on a house when she's old enough is

title: CNBC 调查显示，员工无法就初级员工是否应该在工作中使用人工智能达成一致
content:
初级员工是否应该在工作中使用人工智能？据 CNBC 和周四发布的 SurveyMonkey 季度人工智能和就业调查显示，他们的同事在这个问题上存在分歧。

调查显示，大约 42% 的员工表示应允许初级员工在工作中使用人工智能，并有明确的指导方针和限制，而 35% 的人表示应禁止初级员工使用该技术。该调查于 7 月 22 日至 7 月 22 日至 16 日对美国各地的 1,686 名学生和员工进行了调查。 27. 另有 14% 的受访者表示，初级员工只能在经过监督和批准的情况下使用人工智能，9% 的受访者表示，他们应该能够不受任何限制地自由使用人工智能。

这个问题很棘手：许多雇主正在推动员工培养人工智能技能，希望他们的工作效率更高，但对于职业阶梯较低层的员工来说，有独特的考虑。

入门级工作通常被认为更有可能被中断或取代通过人工智能。根据 ZipRecruiter 7 月份的报告，近三分之一的雇主表示人工智能提高了他们入门级职位的经验要求。入门级求职者还面临着更激烈的职位竞争。

许多年龄在 14 岁到 29 岁之间的 Z 世代成员“对 [AI] 对工作场所的意义不冷不热，”全国大学与雇主协会主席兼首席执行官 Shawn VanDerziel 表示。在 CNBC 的调查中，42% 的 Z 世代受访者表示，应禁止初级员工在工作中使用人工智能，这一比例比接受调查的任何其他一代人都要高。

早期职业员工也可能会因为在大学被禁止使用人工智能而突然被强烈鼓励在工作中使用人工智能而感到痛苦，VanDerziel 表示：他们中的一些人“因为在学校被告知的内容而害怕被抓到‘作弊’。”

人工智能可以他说，人工智能对一些入门级工作很有用，包括委派日常任务、校对、分析大数据集，以及回答常见的工作场所问题，以填补年轻员工刚起步时的技能或资源差距。

但 VanDerziel 警告说，在其他一些类型的任务上使用人工智能可能会让年轻员工倒退，例如在不先学习如何自己完成任务的情况下自动执行任务，或者将决策外包给人工智能。

如果早期职业员工不自己做这些工作，他说，“他们并没有磨练那些有益的工作技能，这些技能可以为其他工作奠定基础。”他补充说，尽管人工智能可能提供了一条现在很方便的“捷径”，但反复依赖它可能会阻止这些工人在某个主题上发展专业知识。

担心人工智能可能会阻碍年轻工人的专业发展，这可能是他们和他们的同事支持对谁可以在工作中使用该技术进行保护或限制的原因之一。员工还可能担心年轻员工提交“AI 工作失败”或包含虚假或误导性信息的输出，导致同事需要做更多工作来修复这些错误。

另一个潜在的担忧：根据 CNBC 5 月份发布的一项调查，37% 的员工将隐私作为他们避免使用人工智能的原因，他们可能担心最缺乏经验的同事可能会意外泄露专有或敏感信息。

人工智能素养可能会吸引许多人VanDerziel 说，批判性思维、沟通和协作仍然经常是雇主在 NACE 的初级员工技能清单中最看重的技能，因此年轻员工也应该注重培养这些技能。

“公司正在将这些新毕业生视为未来的领导者，他们希望为未来提供一条管道。” “即使在人工智能时代，这些技能仍然存在，”他说，并且“在今天更加重要。”
